1 
 
REPORT 
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Ports, 
Shipping and Waterways on the recommendations/observations as contained in its 377th Report 
on ‘Demands for Grants (2025-26) of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways which was 
presented to both the Houses of Parliament.  
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 4th August, 2025 in respect 
of all the recommendations/observations contained in the Report. The replies have been 
categorized as follows:-    
Chapter-I:  
Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Ministry:  
Paragraph Nos.: 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 9, 10, 11, 16, 19, 22.2.  
Total: 9 
 
Chapter-II:  
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the 
replies of the Ministry:  
Paragraph Nos.: 8.4, 12, 14, 20, 20.1, 21, 21.1, 22, 22.1, 23 24, 24.1, 25, 25.1, 25.2, 25.3, 26.3, 
29, 30.  
Total: 19 
 
 
Chapter-III: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have 
not been accepted by the Committee:  
Paragraph Nos.: 26.1, 26.2, 31.  
Total: 3 
 
Chapter-IV: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the final replies of the 
Ministry are still awaited:  
Paragraph Nos.: Nil.  
Total: 0 
 
3.  The Committee desires that final reply in respect of the 
recommendation/observation which has been categorized as interim reply by the 
Committee should be furnished at the earliest. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Committee recommends immediate attention to the challenges facing maritime 
container movement schedules due to global disruptions and trade volatility. The 
Committee strongly urges the Ministry to implement comprehensive digital tracking 
platforms for real-time monitoring of container movements across all major ports. 
Furthermore, the Committee recommends establishing a dedicated Maritime Response 
Unit to address contingencies arising from geopolitical disruptions along key shipping 
routes. The Committee believes these measures are essential to mitigate extended lead 
times currently affecting Asia-Europe shipments and to reduce congestion at strategic port 
hubs.  
(Para 8.1)   
Reply of the Ministry   
1.1 In alignment with the Committee’s recommendations, the Ministry is actively assessing 
the implementation of comprehensive digital tracking platforms to enhance real-time monitoring 
of container movements across all major ports. These efforts align with our broader objective of 
leveraging technology to improve supply chain efficiency and transparency.  
Furthermore, the Ministry acknowledges the strategic significance of establishing a 
dedicated Maritime Response Unit to ensure timely and coordinated responses to geopolitical 
disruptions along key shipping routes. As part of this initiative, the Ministry is evaluating 
potential frameworks for enhancing resilience in maritime logistics and optimizing trade routes 
to safeguard India’s shipping interests. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee notes the ambitious targets under Maritime India Vision 2030 and 
recommends accelerated implementation of mechanization initiatives at all major ports to 
achieve the sub-20-hour turnaround time goal. The Committee strongly advises prioritizing 
budget allocation for modernizing port infrastructure, particularly automated cargo 
handling systems and digital documentation processes. The Committee further 

3 
 
recommends quarterly performance reviews of port efficiency metrics with standardized 
benchmarks to ensure measurable progress toward capacity enhancement targets. 
(Para 8.2)   
 
Reply of the Ministry   
 
2.1 The Ministry acknowledges the Committee’s recommendation for the accelerated 
implementation of mechanisation initiatives across all major ports. In FY 2024–25, the median 
container turnaround time at major ports was recorded at 26.2 hours. Over the past five years, 
major ports in India have undertaken capital expenditure amounting to ₹14,080 crore through 
Internal and Extra Budgetary Resources (IEBR) and Gross Budgetary Support (GBS), along with 
an additional ₹8,898 crore through Public-Private Partnership (PPP) projects. These investments 
have been directed towards comprehensive port modernisation, capacity enhancement for 
handling large volumes of cargo, and the development of port-led industrialisation initiatives 
aimed at streamlining operations and improving overall efficiency. The Ministry also conducts 
regular monthly reviews of key port efficiency parameters to ensure continuous performance 
monitoring and improvement. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
3. The Committee emphasizes that inadequate multi-modal connectivity remains a 
significant bottleneck affecting port efficiency. The Committee recommends establishing a 
dedicated Inter-Ministerial Coordination Cell to expedite port connectivity projects under 
PM Gati Shakti. With reference to 10 Paradip Port, the Committee recommends 
immediate completion of pending railway linkage projects and upgradation of NH-53A to 
facilitate smoother cargo evacuation. The Committee strongly urges synchronized planning 
between the Ministries of Railways, Road Transport and Highways, and Ports, Shipping 
and Waterways to ensure infrastructure development aligns with projected cargo volumes. 
The Committee recommends that the Paradip Port development model be replicated across 
other major ports to enhance seamless connectivity and reduce logistics costs. 
(Para 8.3)   
 
 

4 
 
Reply of the Ministry   
3.1 The Ministry acknowledges the Committee’s observations regarding multi-modal 
connectivity challenges affecting port efficiency. Strengthening infrastructure linkages remains a 
key priority, particularly under the PM Gati Shakti initiative, which is designed to facilitate 
synchronized planning across multiple sectors, ensuring seamless cargo movement and reduced 
logistics costs. 
In alignment with the Committee’s recommendations, the Department for Promotion of Industry 
and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is leading inter-ministerial coordination efforts to expedite 
connectivity projects and ensure alignment with projected cargo volumes. Through DPIIT’s 
leadership, coordination among the Ministries of Railways, Road Transport and Highways, and 
Ports, Shipping and Waterways has been streamlined to accelerate infrastructure development 
and optimize multimodal logistics solutions. 
Regarding Paradip Port, the Ministry remains committed to the timely completion of pending 
railway linkage projects and the upgradation of NH-53A, recognizing their strategic importance 
in facilitating efficient cargo evacuation. These initiatives are being fast-tracked to enhance 
operational capacity, improve trade facilitation, and bolster India’s maritime connectivity 
framework. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
4. The Committee appreciates the Government’s continued emphasis on portled 
economic development which is reflected in the budgetary outlay of ₹866 crore for the 
Sagarmala Programme, inclusive of ₹30 crores for Community Development and ₹24.10 
crore for administrative expenditure. At the same time, however, it recommends that a 
comprehensive impact assessment of Sagarmala projects be conducted, to ensure that 
investments are directly correlated with economic growth, employment generation, and 
infrastructural improvements. Future funding for Sagarmala Programme should be tied to 
performance-based outcomes, with a clear roadmap for project execution timelines and 
transparent reporting mechanisms.  
(Para 9)   
Reply of the Ministry:-  
4.1 The recommendations of the Hon’ble Committee have been duly noted. 
 

5 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
5. The Committee observes that the allocation of ₹ 15 crore for the Inland Water 
Transport - North Eastern Region (IWT-NER) appears disproportionately low given the 
vast potential of inland waterways as a cost-effective and environmentally sustainable 
mode of transport. It did note the investment of ₹ 1,752.31 crore in inland water transport 
infrastructure which would go a long way in strengthening the waterway connectivity. The 
Committee, therefore recommends that a dedicated Inland Waterway Corridor 
Development Plan be instituted, which will ensure that investments extend beyond mere 
infrastructural augmentation to include operational efficiency, multimodal logistics 
integration, and cargo handling capabilities. A periodic review mechanism must be 
established to assess the effectiveness of these investments in enhancing inland navigability 
and economic viability. 
 (Para 10)   
Reply of the Ministry of the Ministry     
5.1 The allocation of ₹ 15 crore is for the Central Sector Schemes for Inland Water Transport 
- North Eastern Region (IWT-NER) under which works are being executed by the concerned 
States on their inland waterways. For the development of cost-effective and environmentally 
sustainable mode of transport on National Waterways (NWs) of NER through Inland Waterways 
Authority of India (IWAI), an investment of Rs. 421 cr. is proposed under BE 2025-26 under 
Capital outlay in North Eastern Areas- Inland Waterways Authority of India. 
In line with the recommendations of the Committee, for the development of a regional 
waterways network integrated with road and rail, the Regional Waterway Grid (RWG) project is 
proposed. The broad objective of the RWG project is to enhance economic activity in the region 
by facilitating trade and commerce via efficient movement of goods and passengers by 
augmenting waterways, putting in place connectivity in a manner that is socially, 
environmentally, and economically sustainable. 
A robust weekly/fortnightly/monthly review mechanism has been established at regional/ 
organizational /ministerial level for effective implementation of works being executed by IWAI 
for close monitoring and targeted progress. 
 
 

6 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
6. The Committee is happy to note the allocation of ₹100.62 crore to the Indian 
Maritime University (IMU) which it believes reflects a commendable commitment on the 
part of the Government to maritime education and workforce development. However, the 
Committee notes with concerns the relatively modest provision of crore for the Tariff 
Authority for Major Ports (TAMP), as it may affect its ability to effectively regulate port 
tariffs in an increasingly complex maritime economy. The Committee therefore 
recommends strengthening regulatory capabilities within TAMP, so that it is equipped 
with the necessary financial and technological resources to maintain an effective regulatory 
framework.  
(Para 11)   
 
 
Reply of the Ministry  
6.1 The Ministry appreciates the Committee’s recognition of the Government’s commitment 
to maritime education and workforce development through the allocation of ₹100.62 crore to the 
Indian Maritime University (IMU). This investment underscores our dedication to fostering high-
quality training, research, and capacity-building to strengthen India’s maritime sector. 
Regarding the observations on the Tariff Authority for Major Ports (TAMP), the Ministry would 
like to clarify that with the enforcement of the Major Port Authorities (MPA) Act, 2021, on 
November 3, 2021, TAMP's tariff-setting functions have been withdrawn. In accordance with the 
new legislative framework, the Central Government is in the process of constituting an 
Adjudicatory Board, which will assume adjudicatory functions as outlined in the Act. This 
transition aims to enhance transparency, efficiency, and responsiveness in port tariff regulation, 
ensuring a robust framework aligned with evolving industry dynamics.   
 
Recommendation/Observation  
7. The Committee, upon examination of the financial allocations and expenditure 
trends under the Sagarmala Programme, notes that while the Budget Estimate (BE) for 
2025-26 has been set at ₹ 810 crore which is a 26.6% increase from the previous year’s BE 
of ₹ 640 crore, there are concerns regarding fund utilisation efficiency. In 2024-25, the 
Revised Estimate (RE) was marginally increased to ₹ 649 crore, but actual expenditure, as 
of date, stands at ₹ 566 crore, reflecting an 87.2% utilisation rate. In the opinion of the 
Committee, there seems to be delays in project execution, or administrative inefficiencies, 

7 
 
which, if left unaddressed, may hinder the full realisation of the ambitious programme’s 
intended objectives. The Committee, therefore, urges the Ministry to ensure greater 
financial discipline and proactive project monitoring to facilitate timely and effective 
utilisation of allocated resources. It is recommended that a comprehensive review be 
undertaken to identify and rectify procedural impediments that have contributed to 
underutilisation in 2024-25, ensuring that the ₹ 810 crore allocated for 2025-26 is expended 
in a structured and time-bound manner. Furthermore, the Committee stresses the 
importance of accurate budget forecasting to minimise the need for midyear revisions and 
recommends that the Ministry strengthen its project implementation framework, including 
regular financial performance reviews and enhanced inter-agency coordination, to uphold 
fiscal prudence and programme efficacy. 
(Para 16)   
Reply of the Ministry     
7.1 The Ministry acknowledges the Committee’s recommendations and is committed to 
ensuring greater financial discipline and proactive project monitoring for effective utilisation of 
the allocated budget for 2025–26. The Ministry is strengthening its project implementation 
framework through regular financial performance reviews and enhanced inter-agency 
coordination. These measures aim to uphold fiscal prudence and ensure timely execution of 
projects in alignment with the Committee’s valuable guidance. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
8. The Committee observes imbalance between capital investments (₹994.33 crore for 
JMVP) and maintenance expenditure (₹267 crore) which in its opinion reflects a critical 
concern in infrastructure development strategy. The Jal Marg Vikas Project, currently 
extended to 2026 with World Bank support, represents a substantial commitment to 
expanding the inland waterway infrastructure along National Waterway-1. While the 
project has demonstrated progress in creating multi-modal terminals at Varanasi, 
Sahibganj, and Haldia, evidence suggests implementation challenges persist, with certain 
tenders being cancelled due to significantly higher bids than estimated values. The 
Committee notes that maintenance expenditure forms the backbone of any sustainable 
infrastructure network, particularly for waterways where regular dredging and channel 
maintenance are essential for ensuring navigability. The current allocation of ₹267 crore 
for maintaining existing waterways appears insufficient, especially when considered against 
the extensive network of 111 National Waterways. The experience from European 
waterway management indicates that sustained maintenance funding is crucial for 

8 
 
ensuring the reliability and performance of inland navigation infrastructure. The 
Committee therefore recommends a more 19 strategic approach involving implementation 
of a Life-Cycle Cost Assessment (LCCA) framework for waterway infrastructure that 
balances initial capital expenditure with long-term maintenance requirements. This 
framework should incorporate detailed assessment of annual maintenance needs for each 
operational waterway segment, ensuring sufficient allocation for critical activities like 
dredging campaigns, navigation aids maintenance, and terminal upkeep. The Ministry 
should establish a minimum maintenance-to-capital expenditure ratio of 1:2 for mature 
waterways, gradually transitioning to 1:1 as the network stabilizes, ensuring sustainable 
operation while continuing necessary expansion  
(Para 19)   
 
Reply of the Ministry of the Ministry     
8.1 As recommended by the Committee, a more strategic approach involving implementation 
of a Life-Cycle Cost Assessment (LCCA) framework for waterway infrastructure that balances 
initial capital expenditure with long-term maintenance requirement, is noted for compliance, at 
planning stage. 
Further, when the waterway regime gets stability, a minimum maintenance-to-capital 
expenditure ratio of 1:2 for mature waterways will be maintained as recommended by the 
Committee. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
13. Furthermore, the Ministry should reform the concession framework for waterway 
operations to offer more attractive risk-sharing arrangements. This includes implementing 
flexible concession periods tied to actual traffic achievement rather than fixed timelines, 
establishing minimum revenue guarantees for pioneer routes, and creating streamlined 
regulatory clearance mechanisms for waterway projects through a single-window system.  
(Para 22.2)   
Reply of the Ministry     
13.1 Noted for compliance. 
 
****  
     

9 
 
CHAPTER-II 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Committee notes that the allocation of ₹0.71 crore for Research & Development 
(R&D) in port development is strikingly low, especially considering the critical role that 
technological advancement plays in ensuring the competitiveness and efficiency of the 
country’s maritime infrastructure. The Committee strongly recommends a significant 
augmentation of R&D funding to bring out innovation in port infrastructure, automation, 
and environmental sustainability. 
(Para 8.4)   
Reply of the Ministry:-  
1.1 The Ministry acknowledges the Committee’s observations regarding the allocation for 
Research & Development (R&D) in port development and recognizes the pivotal role of 
technological advancement in enhancing maritime infrastructure, operational efficiency, and 
environmental sustainability. 
As part of the Ministry’s long-term strategy to modernize port operations, we remain committed 
to fostering innovation in port automation, green technologies, and digital transformation. While 
the current R&D allocation has been set based on existing priorities, the Ministry is actively 
reviewing avenues to augment funding and integrate advanced research methodologies that will 
strengthen India’s maritime competitiveness. 
Efforts are already underway to collaborate with research institutions, technology experts, and 
industry stakeholders to develop innovative solutions that enhance cargo handling efficiency, 
reduce emissions, and improve overall sustainability. The Ministry remains dedicated to ensuring 
that India’s ports continue to evolve in alignment with global best practices and emerging 
technological trends. 
 
 
     
     
     
     

10 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee notes with concern the absence of any direct budgetary allocation 
for the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) and urges the Government to clarify the 
strategic vision for SCI viability and competitive positioning. In the view of the committee, 
it is imperative that a well formulated structured transition plan be put in place to ensure 
minimal disruption to India’s commercial shipping capabilities.  
(Para 12)   
Reply of the Ministry     
2.1 SCI already has  vision and mission as stated below: 
Vision of SCI: To emerge as a team of inspired performers in the field of maritimelogistics, 
Offshore, Port and Terminal Management, serving Indian and global trade. 
Mission of SCI: To serve India’s overseas and coastal seaborne trade as its primary flag carrier, 
while becoming a key player in global maritime logistics by:  
 Maintaining leadership in Indian shipping 
 Building a strong global presence in energy, dry bulk, and niche container shipping 
 Developing reliable, cost-effective business models for emerging maritime opportunities 
 Achieving excellence in quality, health, safety, and environmental systems 
 
SCI has received Budgetary support  in recent years to run various international ferry services. 
Additionally, it is stated that SCI is in the process of formulating a comprehensive long-term 
business plan and based on the same, the financial requirements  sought by SCI, if any,  will be 
looked into by this Ministry. 
 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
3. The Committee observes that the Budget Estimates (BE) for 2025-26 at  ₹ 3,470.58 
crore marks a substantial 45.9% increase over the previous year’s BE of ₹ 2,377.49 crore 
which is the largest annual increase in the past four fiscal years. However, it also notes a 
persistent trend of mid-year budgetary revisions as evident, with Revised Estimates (RE) 
consistently exceeding BE- notably, in 2024-25, RE surged by ₹ 481.05 crore above BE. 
Furthermore, the RE has been declining, with expenditure as a percentage of RE dropping 
from 94.11% in 2022-23 to 86.15% in 2024-25 (as of February 2025) which can either be 

11 
 
due to project execution delays, and possible inefficiencies in financial governance. In the 
opinion of the Committee, given the unprecedented budgetary increase for 2025-26, it 
becomes all the imperative that fiscal discipline is reinforced, fund utilisation is optimised, 
and hurdles in project executions are identified and systematically addressed to prevent a 
further decline in expenditure efficiency.   
 (Para 14)   
Reply of the Ministry     
3.1 The Ministry constantly reviews the project execution and fund utilization. Expenditure 
reported earlier was upto 27.02.2025. However, actual expenditure in FY 2024-25 was Rs 
2837.60 crores which was 99.26 % of RE 2024-25. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
4. The Committee notes the allocation of ₹76.50 crore towards interest payments on 
IWAI bonds and raises concerns about the sustainability of debt-based financing for inland 
waterway projects. While debt instruments provide immediate access to capital necessary 
for infrastructure development, they create rigid fiscal obligations that constrain future 
budgetary flexibility. The current financing structure of the JMVP, with its reliance on 
both international loans (₹2,512 crore from IBRD) and government bonds, exemplifies this 
mixed approach. 
Debt financing offers certain advantages, including preservation of operational autonomy 
and prevention of ownership dilution. However, it also introduces financial covenants that 
may restrict operational flexibility and increases overall financial risk exposure. The 
experience from the financing survey of the inland waterway transport sector indicates that 
while loans on favorable terms remain a preferred financial instrument, there is growing 
interest in alternative financing approaches, particularly among larger operators.  
4.1 The Committee therefore recommends a more balanced financing strategy that  
incorporates diversified funding sources beyond traditional debt instruments. The Ministry 
should develop a Waterway Infrastructure Finance Framework that includes:  
(1) Project-specific revenue bonds tied to direct income streams from waterway operations, 
reducing dependency on general budgetary allocations;  

12 
 
(2) Dedicated Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) specifically for waterway projects 
with stable revenue potential, allowing broader market participation; and  
(3) Blended finance models combining concessional loans, grants, and commercial 
financing to optimize the capital structure for different project components. 
(Para 20 & 20.1)   
Reply of the Ministry     
4.2 The Ministry recognizes the importance of evolving a sustainable and diversified 
financial framework for the Inland Water Transport (IWT) sector. However, it is important to 
contextualize these within the current developmental stage of IWT in India. IWT remains a 
nascent sector with limited commercial maturity and revenue-generating capacity. Unlike sectors 
such as roads and highways, which have seen decades of development, the inland waterways 
sector is still building its foundational infrastructure and operational ecosystem.  
Further, the Ministry is cognizant of the financing challenges across the maritime domain and is 
actively working towards the establishment of Maritime Development Fund (MDF). This fund 
will provide both equity and debt financing tailored to the unique needs of the sector, thereby 
reducing reliance on traditional financial sources. Additionally, the Sagarmala Development 
Company Limited (SDCL) has recently been granted Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) 
status. This strategic development will enable SDCL (Now Sagarmala Finance Corporation 
Limited - SMFCL) to extend debt financing to maritime projects, further strengthening the 
sector’s financial ecosystem.  While the suggestions on revenue bonds, InvITs, and blended 
finance models are Noted, their implementation must be calibrated to the sector’s current 
maturity level. The Ministry remains committed to exploring these instruments progressively, in 
alignment with sectoral growth, investor appetite, and regulatory readiness. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
5. The Committee notes the allocation of ₹421 crore for North-Eastern Region 
infrastructure development targeting NW-2 (Brahmaputra), NW-16 (Barak), and the Indo-
Bangladesh Protocol route which represents a significant opportunity to enhance regional 
connectivity. However, the unique geographical and logistical challenges of the region 
necessitate more nuanced implementation strategies to ensure these investments yield 
meaningful economic returns. In its opinion, stakeholder consultations in the North-
Eastern Region reveal limited awareness about environmental safeguards and coordination 

13 
 
challenges among different agencies involved in riverine infrastructure. Local communities 
prioritize rapid development but lack understanding of the quality standards necessary for 
sustainable waterway operations. Field observations indicate that structural interventions 
like piers, bridges, and river training works can pose navigational hazards when not 
properly coordinated among stakeholders. In order to maximize the effectiveness of the 
₹1,010 crore five-year NER project (2020-2025), the Committee therefore recommends that 
the Ministry implements a Regional Waterway Development Consortium model that brings 
together state governments, local bodies, technical institutions, and private stakeholders in 
a structured governance framework. This consortium should establish a unified project 
monitoring system with standardized reporting protocols and performance 21 indicators 
for all NER waterway projects, enabling real-time tracking of implementation progress 
and rapid intervention where needed. 
(Para 21)   
Reply of the Ministry  
5.1 In the light of recommendation of the Parliament Standing Committee, a National level 
committee viz. Inland Waterway Development Council (IWDC) has been set up under the 
Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways on 12.10.2023 for better 
cooperation and on-boarding of States / UTs in order to accelerate holistic development of Inland 
Water Transport in the country for enhancement of cargo, passenger movement and for river 
cruise tourism. 
As of now, 2 meetings of IWDC have been held at Kolkata and at Kaziranga in which 
announcements regarding development of more waterways including NER states have been 
made.  
 
In the first IWDC meeting with the States / UTs held at Kolkata on 8th January 2024 with 
participation of various States and Stakeholders, two major initiatives were launched in the 
inland waterways sector by Hon'ble Minister of Ports Shipping & Waterways viz. "HaritNauka" 
Guidelines i.e. Green Transition Guidelines for Inland Vessels, and “River Cruise Tourism 
Roadmap 2047". In the meeting, States were requested to study the potential of the waterways 
and devise the action plans for the regulatory and infrastructure development in the respective 
states to realize the potential and to assess the importance of attracting private sector 
participation in the sector to capitalize on the various opportunities.  
 
In the second IWDC meeting held on 10th January, 2025 in Kaziranga, Assam , several 
development activities for waterways, including those in the NER, were announced. Further, to 
facilitate the development of inland waterway projects in the NER, Government has initiated 
proposals from all NER states under the Central Sector Scheme (CSS), with 100% funding 
provided by the Central Government. 
 
 

14 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
6. Furthermore, the Ministry should initiate quarterly multi-stakeholder coordination 
forums in each NER state to harmonize river training works, terminal development, and 
navigation infrastructure planning. These forums should specifically address the 
coordination issues between state Water Resources Departments (WRD) and Inland Water 
Transport (IWT) authorities identified during stakeholder consultations.  
(Para 21.1)   
Reply of the Ministry of the Ministry     
6.1 Regular multi-stakeholder consultation are being done in North Eastern States to promote 
the IWT development. 
Ministry has nominated IWAI as Central Nodal Agency for the projects under Central Sector 
Scheme (CSS). Under the scheme, all the North-Eastern States are being funded for the works 
like river training works, terminal development, and navigation infrastructure etc.  
All the North-Eastern States are being guided through meetings / consultation to formulate the 
projects and to address the issues, if any, regarding IWT developments.  
Recently, the second IWDC meeting took place in Kaziranga, Assam where several development 
activities for waterways in the North Eastern States, were announced and all NE states were 
asked to focus on IWT development.  
Further, more stakeholder consultations will be planned in light of recommendations of 
Parliamentary Standing Committee for the development of IWT infrastructure in NE States. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
7. The Committee further notes the limited engagement of the private sector in inland 
waterway development which in its opinion represents a missed opportunity for 
accelerating infrastructure development while reducing fiscal burden. Despite allocations 
of ₹301 crore for private participation under PPP mode within the JMVP framework, 
actual private investment has remained below expectations. The Ministry’s emphasis on 
nurturing public-private partnerships is indicative of governmental recognition of this gap, 
but systematic structural interventions are needed to translate this intent into action.  
(Para 22)   

15 
 
Reply of the Ministry  
7.1 IWAI's efforts to offer various multimodal terminals such as Varanasi and Sahibganj 
terminals on a PPP basis encountered challenges, such as insufficient traffic for inland water 
transport (IWT), because road and rail were perceived as cheaper options due to the multiple 
handling and multimodal transport requirements of IWT. Issues with Least Available Depth 
(LAD) and first and last mile connectivity also hindered progress.  
However, with initiatives launched recently i.e. ‘Jalvahak’ scheme - a scheme aimed at 
incentivising the movement of long-haul cargo via National Waterways 1 (river Ganga) as well 
as for National Waterways 2 (river Brahmaputra) and National Waterways 16 (river Barak) on 
15th  December 2024 by MoPSW and also the launch of the Fixed Day Scheduled Sailing 
Service that will ply vessels between Kolkata - Patna - Varanasi - Patna - Kolkata stretch of NW 
1 and between Kolkata and Pandu in Guwahati on NW 2 via Indo Bangladesh Protocol Route 
(IBPR)s, the traffic on IWT mode is expected to increase which shall also make the sector more 
attractive for private sector participation. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
8. The Committee therefore urges the Ministry to establish a comprehensive Inland 
Waterway Investment Framework specifically designed to attract private capital across 
multiple segments of the value chain. This framework should include distinct incentive 
structures for three categories of private participation: (1) Infrastructure developers 
focusing on terminal construction, navigation aids, and specialized cargo handling 
facilities; (2) Vessel operators and logistics providers offering transportation services on 
established waterways; and (3) Technology partners bringing innovations in vessel design, 
navigation systems, and environmental solutions. 22 Financial mechanisms should be 
calibrated to address specific barriers faced by different types of private investors. For 
infrastructure developers, enhanced Viability Gap Funding with coverage up to 40% for 
waterway projects in challenging geographies would reduce entry barriers. For vessel 
operators, accelerated depreciation provisions and priority sector lending status would 
stimulate fleet modernization. For technology partners, a dedicated Waterway Innovation 
Fund providing matching grants for pilot deployments would accelerate adoption of new 
solutions.  
(Para 22.1)   
 
 

16 
 
Reply of the Ministry  
8.1 In respect of category (1) & (2) of private participation, the National Waterways 
(Construction of Jetties / Terminals) Regulations 2025 has been notified, allowing private 
companies to invest and operate Inland Waterways infrastructure by providing a clear regulatory 
framework.  
Jal Vahak scheme for providing 35% incentive to promote the utilization of inland waterways 
transport sector by cargo owners and for establishing scheduled service for cargo movement on 
NW-1 and NW-2 and NW-16 via Indo Bangladesh Protocol has been approved by the 
Government.  The scheme is at a cost of Rs. 95.42 crore for three years and can be scaled up or 
modified depending on the success of the scheme. The scheme also aims to start a scheduled 
waterway cargo service between Kolkata and Varanasi/Pandu using IWAI vessels through 
Shipping Corporation of India for demonstration effect and to increase trust of cargo 
movers/owners in the waterway movement. 
In respect of category (3) private participation, Study has been allotted to NTCPWC for 
identifying areas in various States for development of Ship Repair Facilities. Parallely, 
stakeholders have been engaged for development of design suitable for national waterways. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
9. Ship Building and ship repair- The Ministry informed the Committee that to 
promote indigenous shipbuilding industry in India, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and 
Waterways has brought in Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP) scheme for 
Indian shipyards to procure orders from domestic as well as international market and to be 
competitive in international market for securing global orders. The scheme offers financial 
assistance to Indian Shipyards for shipbuilding contracts signed between April 1, 2016 to 
March 31, 2026 with rate of financial assistance starting from 20% in 2016 and diminishing 
to 11% in 2026 with a budget allocation of ₹4000Crore. Also, financial assistance of 30% is 
given for vessels where main propulsion is achieved by means of green fuels such as 
Methanol/ Ammonia / Hydrogen fuel cells and financial assistance of 20% for vessels with 
electric means of propulsion or vessels fitted with hybrid propulsion system. An amount of 
₹ 138Crore has been allocated for SBFAP for FY 2025-26. Funds are projected based on 
tentative delivery of ships by shipyards.  
(Para 23)    
 
 

17 
 
Reply of the Ministry     
9.1 It has been observed by the Committee that an amount of ₹ 138Crore has been allocated 
for SBFAP for FY 2025-26. This figure is for the FY 2024-2025 which has been fully expended. 
The budget allocation for FY 2025-2026 is Rs. 350Cr.  
 
Recommendation/Observation  
10. The Committee notes the allocation of ₹138 crore for shipbuilding assistance in FY 
2025-26 which represents a modest commitment when viewed against the backdrop of the 
scheme's total allocation of ₹4,000 crore that was intended to span from 2016 to 2026. This 
relatively small annual allocation however raises serious concerns about the pace and scale 
of implementation. Evidence suggests that despite the policy being operational for nearly 
nine years, barely 10% of the total corpus has been utilized, indicating structural 
impediments in policy implementation. Since its inception, the SBFAP has facilitated 313 
vessel orders across 39 shipyards, with a cumulative value of approximately ₹10,500 crore. 
However, financial assistance disbursed stands at only ₹337 crore for 135 completed 
vessels. This significant gap between allocated funds and actual disbursement suggests 
systemic issues in fund absorption capacity within the industry. The progressive reduction 
in financial assistance percentages—from 20% in 2016 to the current 11%—appears to 
have contributed to diminishing industry interest in the scheme, particularly as competing 
shipbuilding nations like China and South Korea continue to provide 20-30% subsidies to 
their shipyards. 
10.1 The Committee therefore suggests that the Ministry undertakes a comprehensive 
performance audit of the SBFAP to identify specific bottlenecks preventing optimal fund 
utilization. The audit should examine whether procedural complexities in application 
processing, unrealistic valuation mechanisms, or lack of shipyard capacity are inhibiting 
fund absorption. The web application for processing applications, despite improvements 
made after industry feedback, may require further streamlining to facilitate easier access 
to financial assistance. 
(Para 24 & 24.1)    
Reply of the Ministry     
10.2 It is informed that the funds allocated for SBFAP for FY 2025-26 is Rs. 350 crores. 
(I) The reasons for lower disbursement till date are as under: 

18 
 
(a) At the time of drafting the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy, several major shipyards 
such as Reliance Naval and Engineering Limited, ABG Shipyard, Bharati Shipyard, and Tebma 
Shipyard Limited were operational, with numerous vessels under construction. These shipyards 
represented the bulk of India’s commercial shipbuilding capacity. However, due to multiple 
challenges—including the absence of a shipbuilding subsidy between September 2007 and 
March 2016 —many of these shipyards entered insolvency proceedings under the National 
Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). This led to a substantial decline in India’s shipbuilding 
capacity, reducing it by more than half, and significantly impacting the country’s overall 
shipbuilding capability. 
(b) In addition to the above, the COVID-19 pandemic and its aftermath further affected the 
sector, causing high lead times and extremely low production volumes during the period 2020–
2022. This severely constrained shipbuilding operations nationwide. 
(c) It may also be noted that ship construction is a long-gestation process. Hence, though the 
current policy was introduced in 2016, the first application for financial assistance was received 
only in January 2018. As a result, no disbursements occurred during the initial 1.5 years of 
policy implementation. 
(d) Under the present Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy, approvals are granted in two 
stages. First, an in-principle approval is accorded at the time of signing of the shipbuilding 
contract. Second, the actual disbursement of financial assistance takes place upon the successful 
delivery of the vessel. Accordingly, the applicability and timeline of the policy must be 
interpreted in this framework. While in-principle approvals will be granted until March 31, 2026, 
fund disbursement under these approvals will necessarily extend beyond this date. For instance: 
For regular vessels, which are allowed three year construction period, disbursement may extend 
until March 2029, if the contract is signed in Mar 2026. For specialized vessels, which are 
allowed a six-year construction period, disbursement may extend until Mar 2032, if the contract 
is signed in Mar 2026. 
(e) In this context, it is important to highlight that a significant number of shipbuilding contracts 
were signed in the post-COVID period, reflecting a revival of market confidence and renewed 
interest in domestic shipbuilding. As a result, while the actual disbursement under the policy 
currently stands at approximately 
Rs. 464.15 crore, the committed liability under approved contracts is already estimated at around 
Rs. 2,700 crore. These further underscores the necessity for continued and predictable policy 
support to ensure the long-term sustainability and growth of the shipbuilding sector in India. 
(f) Considering the capital intensive and long gestation nature of shipbuilding, initiatives to boost 
shipbuilding need a stable, long-term perspective to alter the existing market dynamics. 
Accordingly, the impact of the shipbuilding financial assistance policy has taken some time to 
reflect in the increased shipbuilding contracts being signed. 

19 
 
(II) Web Application and processing of fund release applications: 
For the Financial Year 2024–2025, the average time taken for release of funds under the scheme 
has been approximately 60 days. This includes a 30-day window provided to applicant shipyards 
to address any deficiencies or to furnish required clarifications. The current fund disbursement 
process is end-to-end electronic workflow with no manual intervention from the shipyards. 
Nevertheless, to enhance user experience, operational efficiency and a shift to an upgraded 
reporting module, a new and improved digital portal is currently under development. The 
upgraded portal is expected to go live by June 2026. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
11. The Committee observes the current SBFAP framework includes provisions for 
enhanced incentives—30% for vessels powered by green fuels (methanol, ammonia, 
hydrogen) and 20% for those with electric or hybrid propulsion systems. However, without 
a dedicated allocation specifically earmarked for these sustainable technologies within the 
₹138 crore budget for FY 2025-26, there remains a serious risk that traditional 
shipbuilding might continue to dominate fund utilization. As global shipping increasingly 
focuses on decarbonization, India risks falling behind in developing indigenous capabilities 
for green vessel construction. The implications extend beyond environmental 
considerations to encompass future market competitiveness, as regulatory pressures and 
market demands increasingly favor low-emission vessels. The shipping ministry's 
recognition of green vessels in its policy framework indicates awareness of this shift, but 
implementation requires more targeted financial commitment.  
11.1 The Committee further notes the upcoming SBFAP 2.0, with its proposed allocation 
of ₹18,000 crore and enhanced subsidies of 25% for specialized vessels and 30% for green 
vessels, represents a significant step forward. However, this policy requires immediate 
operationalisation with a clear timeline for implementation and specific allocations for 
different vessel categories. The Ministry should establish immediate ring-fencing of at least 
40% of the current year's allocation (approximately ₹55 crore) exclusively for green vessel 
construction, creating a dedicated funding stream that ensures India builds capacity in this 
emerging technology area. 
11.2 The Committee notes that the current practice of projecting SBFAP funds based on 
tentative ship delivery schedules introduces significant inefficiencies in fund utilization. 
Shipbuilding projects, particularly those involving complex vessels, are vulnerable to 
production delays, supply chain disruptions, and technical challenges that can extend 
timelines considerably. This creates a mismatch between projected fund requirements and 

20 
 
actual disbursement schedules, contributing to the observed pattern of underutilization. 
The construction of specialized and green vessels, which involve more complex technologies 
and often require sourcing components from global supply chains, are particularly 
susceptible to such delays. This problem is likely to be exacerbated as Indian shipyards 
expand their capabilities to build more sophisticated vessels with lower emission profiles. 
The Committee feels implementing a milestone-based fund release mechanism would 
fundamentally transform how financial assistance is distributed. Under this approach, 
shipyards would receive predetermined percentages of the total assistance amount upon 
completion of defined construction milestones, such as steel cutting, keel laying, launching, 
and final delivery. This approach would provide shipyards with steady cash flow 
throughout the construction process, rather than concentrating financial support at project 
completion. 
11.3 The Committee therefore urges the Ministry develops a standardized set of 
verifiable milestones for different vessel categories, with appropriate weightage assigned to 
each stage. For instance, the steel cutting stage might trigger release of 15% of the total 
assistance, keel laying another 25%, launching 30%, and final delivery the remaining 30%. 
This structured approach would maintain financial pressure on shipyards to progress 
systematically while providing them with the liquidity needed to finance ongoing 
construction. 
(Para 25, 25.1, 25.2 & 25.3)   
Reply of the Ministry     
11.4 The policy was amended in Aug 2023, to include higher financial Assistance for 
green/electric/hybrid vessels. Accordingly, in-principle approvals have been granted to such 
vessels and accordingly, based on the delivery schedule of such vessels, funds have already been 
allocated in the respective year’s budget estimates. Hence, it is submitted that the funding for all 
green/hybrid/electric vessels have been duly accounted based on the inputs received from 
respective shipyards. 
11.5 Fund is released only on the basis of actual delivery schedule of the vessels already given 
in-principle approval. SBFAP 2.0 is under submission for cabinet approval. 
11.6 Stage payments are considered in the SBFAP 2.0 on the basis of major milestones. SBFAP 
2.0 is currently under submission for cabinet approval. 
 
 

21 
 
12. To address the persistent challenges in fund disbursement and project tracking, the 
Ministry should implement an integrated digital monitoring framework that provides real-
time visibility into project progress across all SBFAP-supported shipbuilding activities. 
This system should incorporate automated milestone verification through digital 
documentation, physical inspections, and timestamped visual evidence of construction 
progress. The framework should include a quarterly performance dashboard accessible to 
all stakeholders, including the Ministry, shipyards, and oversight bodies. This dashboard 
would track key performance indicators such as funds allocated, milestones achieved, 
disbursements made, and potential bottlenecks. Regular performance reviews based on this 
data would enable proactive intervention where projects show signs of delay.  
(Para 26.3)   
 
Reply of the Ministry     
12.1 Real time broad metrics regarding, registration of shipyards (Approved, under-process, 
rejected), In-principal application (Approved, under-process, rejected) and fund application 
(Approved, under-process, rejected) is already available on the portal www.shipbuilding.nic.in 
for the public to view. Also, Sagarmanthan data is being regularly updated to provide real time 
performance review by MoPSW. Further, the new portal being developed by DGS for the 
implementation of the SBFAP policy will also provide separate access to MoPSW with specific 
screen to monitor real time progress including quarterly performance dashboard and visibility on 
funds disbursed to shipyards in their respective login. Further, PFMS integration is envisaged in 
the development of the new portal, which will show the real time updates on disbursal of funds 
without necessitating manual interventions. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
13. The Committee has undertaken an assessment of the budgetary allocation for the 
Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL) for FY 2025-26, amounting to 
₹ 565 crore. It notes that as the DGLL operates as a self-sustaining entity, funding its 
revenue expenditure (₹ 475 crore) through navigation dues 29 collected (₹ 475 crore) and 
meeting its capital expenditure (₹ 90 crore) from reserve funds, it also makes DGLL highly 
dependent on stable maritime traffic for revenue generation. Any decline in international 
shipping activity could adversely impact its financial sustainability and restrict future 
capital investments.The Committee recommends that DGLL adopts a more diversified 
financial approach to secure resilience and ensure uninterrupted modernisation of India’s 

22 
 
marine navigation infrastructure. It may conduct a comprehensive risk assessment to 
evaluate potential fluctuations in revenue collection due to global shipping trends, 
economic downturns, or geopolitical disruptions; explore alternative revenue-generation 
mechanisms, including collaborations with private maritime stakeholders and leveraging 
DGLL’s expertise for international consultancy services, and should consider establishing a 
contingency reserve fund to mitigate financial instability during periods of reduced 
revenue collection.  
(Para 29)   
 
Reply of the Ministry     
13.1 The observations of the committee are noted and the following details are submitted for 
kind consideration: 
• DGLL is a self-sustaining organization, and its revenue expenditures are met from the 
receipts of Marine Aids to Navigation Dues and its capital expenditures are met from its own 
Reserve Funds.  
• DGLL being an organization under the Government of India, its receipts are deposited 
with the Consolidated Fund of India (CFI) and expenditures are being met from the allocated 
budget through Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) of Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. 
• A comparative statement of revenue receipts for the last 5 years and % of variation with 
respect to previous year may be seen in Annexure-I. 
• From the data given in Annexure-I, it is evident that a stable and largely upward trend is 
evident in the revenue generation for DGLL over the years, even recovering positively after 
occasional short-term declines due to exceptional circumstances (e.g., COVID-19 pandemic). 
The recent consistent growth reflects a robust and resilient revenue model. 
• DGLL is maintaining 02 reserve funds namely “General Reserve Fund“ and 
“Depreciation Reserve Fund”. Annual contribution to these reserve funds is strategically planned 
to meet the long-term capital investment in future projects and financial sustainability. 
• The operational and financial performance, including revenue status of DGLL are 
periodically reviewed by the Central Advisory Committee for Marine Aids to Navigation 
(CACAtoN) which is a consultative body constituted under the provision of the Marine Aids to 
Navigation Act, 2021. This committee is headed by Secretary (MoPSW) and comprises of 

23 
 
Hon’ble Members of Parliament, Senior officials from Government of India and maritime 
stakeholders including private associations.  
• Additionally, provisions under the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021 empowers the 
Central Government, in consultation with CACAtoN, to revise and increase the Marine Aids to 
Navigation Dues if any revenue shortfall is anticipated. This mechanism ensures financial 
resilience against any unexpected economic downturns.

Recommendation/Observation  
14. The Committee further notes that the ₹ 90 crore capital outlay is mainly allocated 
towards development of new lighthouses, implementation of remote monitoring systems for 
navigation aids, establishment of a new Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) at Port Blair, and 
Integration of Vessel Traffic Management Systems (VTMS) across major ports. However, 
there is limited clarity on project timelines, cost efficiency, and expected impact. The 
Committee therefore recommends the Ministry to provide detailed project implementation 
roadmaps with timelines, performance benchmarks, projected outcomes for capital 
projects, and see to a timely completion of VTMS integration.  
(Para 30)   
 
Reply of the Ministry     
14.1 Detailed project implementation roadmap has been prepared and may be seen in 
Annexure-II.

25 
 
 
CHAPTER-III 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF 
THE MINISTRY HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Ministry should conduct an urgent review of anticipated fund requirements for the 
remainder of FY 2025-26, identifying shipyards with confirmed orders that can demonstrate 
clear progress toward delivery milestones. Unutilized funds from the broader ₹4,000 crore 
allocation should be systematically redistributed to support these viable projects, ensuring 
maximum resource utilization before the current scheme expires in 2026. This reallocation 
should prioritize yards that have demonstrated consistent delivery performance and those 
engaged in constructing specialized or green vessels that align with future maritime needs. The 
experience gained from the previous shipbuilding financial assistance scheme, which has 
supported 135 delivered vessels, provides sufficient data to identify high-performing shipyards 
that can effectively utilize additional funding.   
 (Para 26.1)   
Reply of the Ministry     
1.1 Budget estimates for FY 2025-26 has accounted for all ships (green/others) for which an 
application is expected to be made (subsequent to the delivery of the vessel) in this financial 
year. Also, funds disbursed to green/hybrid/electric vessels under SBFAP would be separately 
accessible in the new portal. 
 
Further Recommendations/Observations 
1.2 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should cross-verify the basis 
on which anticipated applications for FY 2025-26 have been estimated. Since actual 
applications are submitted only post-delivery, the Committee stresses the need for a robust 
verification mechanism to avoid over- or under-estimation of fund requirements, thereby 
ensuring realistic budgeting. 
 

26 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. Beyond simply allocating a portion of existing funds to green vessel construction, the 
Ministry should establish a dedicated Green Shipbuilding Innovation Fund within the SBFAP 
framework. This fund would finance not only vessel construction but also research and 
development activities focused on adapting international green shipping technologies to Indian 
conditions. The proposed SBFAP 2.0, with its enhanced subsidies for green vessels, creates an 
opportunity to institutionalize this approach. The fund should support collaborative projects 
between shipyards, research institutions, and technology providers to develop standardized 
designs for green vessels suited to Indian operational contexts. This would create a pipeline of 
technically validated vessel designs that Indian shipyards could offer to domestic and 
international clients at competitive prices.  
(Para 26.2)   
Reply of the Ministry     
2.1 In November 2021, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) released 
five variants of Approved Standardized Tug Designs (ASTDS) for use by major ports. These 
designs aim to streamline procurement processes and encourage construction within Indian 
shipyards. Further, Green Tug transition program(GTTP) and Green craft transition program 
(GCTP) have been implemented to ensure demand driven greener transition. 
 
 
Further Recommendations/Observations 
2.2 The Committee further recommends that the Green Tug Transition Programme 
(GTTP) and Green Craft Transition Programme (GCTP) be integrated with a long-term 
assured demand framework, whereby major ports, PSUs and inland waterway authorities 
commit to phased procurement targets for green vessels, thereby providing order visibility 
and reducing investment risks for Indian shipyards. 
 
 
 

27 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
3. The Committee observes that ₹ 475 crore revenue outlay is directed towards general 
administration of DGLL, operation and maintenance of maritime navigation aids, management 
of the Vessel Traffic Service at Gulf of Kachchh (VTSGOK), and upkeep of lighthouse tender 
vessels. It acknowledges that though these allocations support day-to-day functionality, there is a 
need for increased 30 investment in technological upgrades and human resource capacity-
building to bring the country’s marine navigation systems at par with international best 
practices. The Committee recommends that the Ministry allocate a greater proportion of revenue 
towards technological modernisation, particularly in automation of aids to navigation and 
regular training and capacity-building programmes for DGLL personnel to ensure efficient 
utilisation of advanced maritime technologies.   
(Para 31)   
Reply of the Ministry     
3.1 Revenue Expenditure is utilized for technological modernisation and capacity building at 
MNTI which conducts International and domestic trainings as detailed below: 
I. Enhancement of Navigational Services: A continuous improvement plan has been 
instituted that includes periodic audits, training programs to ensure that the DGLL remains 
aligned with international best practices in maritime navigation.  Additionally, funds under the 
Capital Head are strategically utilized for the technological modernization of Aids to Navigation 
(AtoN) infrastructure. 
II. MNTI, Kolkata has Scheduled international training on: 
 IWRAP Risk Assessment tool for international participants is scheduled on 07th July 2025 
to 11th July 2025  
 Level-1 AtoN manager training course from 27th Oct-2025 to 21st Nov-2025 
 Several training programs are planned during 2025–26 for domestic stakeholders and 
departmental officials to enhance technical and operational competencies. 
 
 
Further Recommendations/Observations 
3.2 While taking note of the Ministry’s assurance regarding training initiatives at the 
Maritime Navigation Training Institute (MNTI), the Committee recommends that a 
structured multi-year capacity-building roadmap be prepared for DGLL personnel, clearly 
identifying skill gaps in emerging technologies such as e-Navigation, AI-based vessel traffic 
monitoring, remote AtoN management, and cyber security of navigation systems. 

28

CHAPTER-I 
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE MINISTRY 
  
DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2025-26) 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee acknowledges the Ministry's commitment to infrastructure 
development but emphasizes the necessity for enhanced financial oversight, timely 
project execution, and rigorous quality control standards. It recommends establishing a 
comprehensive and independent monitoring framework, supported by advanced project 
management technologies and regular audits, to proactively address delays in land 
acquisition, regulatory approvals, and contractor inefficiencies. Additionally, the 
Committee advises careful and strategic management of asset monetization initiatives to 
safeguard long-term revenue sustainability without compromising future income 
streams.  
 (Para 7) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 MoRTH has institutionalized independent online monitoring framework for addressing 
the delay in Land Acquisition, Environment & Forest Clearance and GAD for ROBs/RUBs 
approval.  
1.2 The complete Land acquisition process has been made online through Bhoomi Rashi 
Portal by leveraging the technology.3,200+ projects have been facilitated, covering over 
145,000 hectares of land and issuing 13,500+ gazette notifications. This has enabled direct 
transfer of Rs. 19,500 Cr to landowners, reducing leakages and also eliminating the need for 
Rs. 27,000 Cr. of float funds in CALA accounts. Overall, LA process has been shortened by 
~3 months, thus significantly improving efficiency and transparency. 
1.3 MoEF&CC has developed the Parivesh Portal 2.0 and customized for MoRT&H 
providing a single-window system for monitoring and managing environmental, forest, 
wildlife, and CRZ clearances. This enabled tracking the online status of clearances which 
helps in early Forest and Wildlife clearances. With real-time dashboards, color-coded alerts 
for delays, and a three-tier oversight structure, it ensures faster, transparent and accountable 
clearance processes while reducing bottlenecks. Analysis of delay shows that 75% of the 
delay is at State level and 25% is at central level. 
1.4 Similarly, MoRTH and the Ministry of Railways jointly launched RoB/RUB Portal, in 
July 2025, to centralize approvals for Road Over Bridges and Road Under Bridges. The 
portal sets fixed timelines for approvals, reducing the time for GADs from 70 to 50 days, 

- 3 - 
 
structural drawings to 11 days (plus 7 after compliance), and launching schemes and 
QAP/WPSS approvals within 30 days. With role-based access, dashboards, and auto-
notifications, the portal ensures predictable, time-bound approvals and closer coordination 
between highway and railway agencies. 
1.5 Data Lake MIS is MoRT&H’s in-house project and contract management system that 
enables continuous project monitoring, payment tracking and dispute resolution. Provides 
real-time project monitoring through GIS-enabled dashboards and customized reports for 
senior management. Accountability is ensured at all levels, from concessionaires and 
consultants to PIUs, regional offices, and headquarters, with automated alerts highlighting 
pending actions. Includes a dispute resolution module to ensure timely redressal of contractor 
and stakeholder issues.  
1.6 Together, these platforms form a cohesive digital stack that supports MoRTH’s vision 
for efficient National Highway development. By digitizing key processes across the lifecycle 
from land acquisition and clearances to implementation and monitoring, MoRTH has 
significantly improved project delivery and stakeholder coordination. 
1.7 Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs authorized MoRTH / NHAI to monetize 
public funded NH projects which are operational and are generating toll revenues for at least 
two years (which was later reduced to one year) after the Commercial Operations Date 
(COD) subject to approval of the Competent Authority in MoRTH/NHAI. Cabinet also 
approved the proposal to authorize MoRTH / NHAI to set up Infrastructure Investment Trust 
(InvIT) and monetize completed and operational NH projects. NHAI is also authorized to 
raise long term finance from banks by securitizing user fee receipts from toll plazas as an 
alternate mode of asset monetization.  
1.8 Accordingly, MoRTH through NHAI monetizes assets through three modes – Toll 
Operate & Transfer (ToT), InvIT, and Securitization [Project based Financing through 
Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)]. Under ToT and InvIT, operational assets with stable cash 
flow are offered to investors, freeing them from pre-construction and construction risks. The 
concessionaires are exposed to revenue risk and operations and maintenance obligations. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The relatively small reduction in maintenance funding (Rs.4,595 crore allocated 
against Rs.4,695 crore projected) may seem insignificant but requires deeper analysis. 
Research indicates that when agencies attend to routine maintenance (filling potholes, 
maintaining pavement edges) but neglect periodic maintenance and rehabilitation, they 
may save money in the short term but eventually face expensive reconstruction costs. 
(Para 16) 

- 4 - 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Ministry should transform its approach to maintenance by implementing a 
comprehensive 10-step maintenance planning process that includes facility audits, task 
definition, prioritization, scheduling, resource allocation, implementation, safety 
protocols, performance metrics, emergency preparedness, and documentation. This 
structured approach would ensure that maintenance budgets, though slightly reduced, 
deliver optimal outcomes through strategic targeting and efficient execution. 
(Para 16.1) 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. For effective implementation, the Ministry should develop a digitized asset 
management system that tracks the condition of all national highways and predicts 
maintenance needs based on traffic patterns, climate conditions, and construction 
materials. This system should prioritize maintenance based on safety concerns, 
economic importance, and cost-effectiveness rather than simply responding to visible 
deterioration. Furthermore, maintenance contracts should incorporate performance-
based incentives that reward contractors for maintaining high-quality road conditions 
rather than merely completing specified activities. 
(Para 16.2) 
Reply of the Ministry (2 to 4, above) 
4.1 Maintenance expenditure in the ongoing works which are ongoing and during Defect 
Libility Period / Concession period of Projects under EPC/HAM/BOT/TOT/INvIT are taken 
up the respective Contractor and Concessionaire. Such expenditure are not included in the 
MoRTH expenditure statement as these expenditure are not being done through Government 
Budget 
 
4.2 For all remaining sections of NHs stretches, where DLP has ended or is not under any 
concession period of BOT/HAM/TOT/InvIT project, Government has taken a policy decision 
to undertake maintenance works through Performance Based Maintenance Contract (PBMC) 
or Short Term Maintenance Contract (STMC). While STMC works are generally undertaken 
for a contract period of 1-2 year, PBMC works are undertaken for a contract period of about 
5-7 years. The maintenance work on PBMC mode is in line with the recommendation of the 
committee which ensures minimum performance standards in maintenance with time bound 
defect rectification. Any delay in account of defect rectification attracts automatic penal 
provisions.  
4.3 Year – wise details of expenditure incurred on M&R of such NHs stretches since 
2014-15 onwards is as under:-

Automated and Intelligent Machine-Aided Construction has been adopted which ensures

4.8 Road condition assessment is carried out through Network Survey Vehicle (NSV) for 
the NHs stretches before start of work, before issue of completion certificate and thereafter at 
regular intervals of six months after completion of the work, thereby enabling quality 
assessment of NHs at regular intervals for (i) ensuring the maintenance during Concession

4.9 Further, app based monitoring through National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)

Recommendation/Observation 
5. For effective implementation, the Ministry should develop a digital dashboard 
accessible to all stakeholders that provides real-time updates on project status, fund 
utilization, and achievement of milestones. Each project should have clearly defined 
quarterly targets with automatic escalation procedures if deviations exceed 
predetermined thresholds. This approach ensures early identification of implementation 
challenges and enables prompt corrective action before projects face serious delays. 
(Para 17.1) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
5.1 MoRTH has developed online project monitoring portals (Data lake used by NHAI 
and Project Monitoring & Information System (PMIS) used by all other implementing 
agencies) in which access to dashboard is provided to all implementing agencies for getting 
real-time updates on achievements vis-à-vis targets, project progress, fund utilization, 
milestone achievement, etc. Development of additional features is underway and the plan is 
to have a single portal accessible to all implementing agencies. Data Lake portal enables 
access to all stakeholders that provides real-time updates on project status, fund utilization, 
and achievement of milestones. Each project should have clearly defined quarterly targets 
with automatic escalation procedures if deviations exceed predetermined thresholds. This 
ensures early identification of implementation challenges and enables prompt corrective 
action before projects face serious delays. 
 
 

- 7 - 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6. The monitoring system should also incorporate emergency preparedness 
elements to address unexpected challenges such as natural disasters, material shortages, 
or contractor defaults. By establishing clear protocols for these contingencies, the 
Ministry can minimize disruption and maintain project momentum even when facing 
unforeseen obstacles. Additionally, comprehensive documentation and training 
procedures should be implemented to ensure institutional memory and consistent 
application of best practices across all projects regardless of individual staffing changes. 
(Para 17.2) 
Reply of the Ministry 
6.1 The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRT&H) has recently notified 
Disaster Management Plan (DMP). The DMP provides comprehensive framework for 
managing disasters with a focus on maintaining and restoring traffic connectivity on roads 
and highways. The institutional framework of MoRT&H shall be laid down under two sub-
plans, one for all disaster events (eg. Landslide, Flood, Earthquake etc.) other than “Road 
Accident” (Volume-I: Overview and Disaster Management Sub-Plan for Highways) and 
"Road Accidents" as Nodal Ministry (Volume-II: Disaster Management Sub-Plan for Road 
Accidents). 
6.2 The document provides a comprehensive and integrated approach of managing 
disasters and reducing risk of disaster, with a clear-cut hierarchy and well assigned roles & 
responsibilities of officers of various agencies of MoRT&H. A Disaster Management 
Division (DM-Div.) headed by Chief Engineer/Joint Secretary level officer has been 
envisaged under this DMP, which shall act as Nodal Division of MoRT&H to coordinate 
with Ministries/Departments of the Central Government, State Government/ District 
Administration as well as executing agencies of MoRT&H. Further, a Standing Committee 
comprising of senior officials of the Ministry has been envisaged and has been assigned with 
the Role to approve policy / guidelines. 
6.3 Further, financial delegation have been assigned at various levels for sanctioning & 
execution of immediate restoration work in the wake of a Disaster event with bare minimum 
time ensuring uninterrupted traffic movement. 
6.4 Also all officers have been sensitized for effectively using the National Database 
for Emergency Management (NDEM) for study of flood pattern, hydrological study and 
Disaster Prone Zone to minimize the adverse impact of eco sensitive areas.

Recommendation/Observation 
7. Furthermore, the Ministry should commission independent third-party audits of 
selected projects to validate internal monitoring data and identify opportunities for 
systemic improvement. These audits should evaluate not just compliance with financial 
and technical specifications but also assess whether projects are delivering anticipated 
economic and social benefits. This external perspective would strengthen accountability 
while providing valuable insights for future planning and implementation. 
 
(Para 17.3) 
Reply of the Ministry 
7.1 As the NH network expanded in the last decade from ~91,000 km to 1.46 Lakh km, 
management and monitoring of NH quality is critical. To ensure standardized monitoring, 
equipment based condition monitoring system to monitor roughness, cracking, rutting, and 
potholes was designed by MoRT&H through Network Survey Vehicle (NSV). NSVs are 
mobile data collection and processing centres with sensors like laser profile meter, laser crack 
measurement system, GPS, 360 video imagery etc. To enable continuous pavement quality 
monitoring, MoRT&H has instituted periodic surveys (once in 6 months) of the NH network 
through Network Survey Vehicle.  A Centralized GIS platform developed for objective 
assessment of pavement condition based on inputs from NSV within 48 hrs. Process planned 
for report generation and responsibility fixing matrix within 10 days. For ensuring third party 
audit, Ministry has started the independent Network Survey Vehicle (NSV) survey for 
ensuring the pavement quality. This independent NSV survey is done apart from the regular 
NSV surveys through Supervision Consultant / Authority Engineer / Independent Engineer 
on the recently completed stretches which are within the defect liability period and also in 
PBMC contracts.  
7.2 MoRT&H has initiated NSV survey of the network, prioritizing the 38,000 km under 
O&M stage with NHAI currently - Phase 1 covering 21,000 km (about 1 Lakh lane km )has 
been completed for 1st round and initiated for 2nd round. Phase 2 covering remaining 17,000 
km of NHAI has been initiated in Oct’25.Government is planning to implement this survey 
PAN INDIA across all agencies.  
7.3 Additionally, Ministry also appoints Third Party Quality Auditors for systematic, 
independent and documented process of investigating the Quality Assurance/ Quality Control 
system of National Highway Projects as per the provisions of IRC: SP: 112-2017. Retired 
Officers from Central / State Government are empanelled as Team Leaders by NHAI and 
Special Project Monitors (SPMs) by NHIDCL for Quality Inspections of NHAI & NHIDCL 

- 10 - 
 
projects respectively. Above empanelled Team Leaders in NHAI / Special Project Monitors

BRO. In addition to quality of works, scope of Third Party Quality Audits covers safety

Recommendations/Observations 
8. The Committee is equally concerned by the lack of an effective emergency 
response system. While noting the pilot implementation of the cashless treatment 
scheme in six states, the Committee finds the pace of expansion inadequate. The 
Committee therefore directed the Ministry to ensure its nationwide rollout as a matter 
of priority, integrating it with a trauma care network along major highways and 
establishing clear coordination protocols between ambulance services, hospitals, and 
enforcement agencies. 
(Para 25) 
Recommendation/Observation 
9. Drawing from established emergency response frameworks, the Ministry should 
implement a four-phase emergency response strategy: detection, notification, response, 
and treatment. This requires developing an observability platform that integrates 
traffic monitoring systems, emergency call centres, ambulance services, and hospital 
trauma units into a unified response network. The cashless treatment scheme should be 
expanded nationwide within 12 months, accompanied by establishment of fully 
equipped trauma care centres at 100-kilometer intervals along all national highways. 
(Para 25.1) 
Reply of the Ministry (8 & 9, above) 
9.1 MoRTH has notified the cashless treatment of road accident victims scheme, 2025 on 
5th May, 2025 in consultation with Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) to 
provide cashless treatment to victims of road accidents in the country. The detailed guidelines 
including process flow, stakeholder wise standard operating procedures and clearly 
delineated roles and responsibilities have also been notified on 4th June, 2025. 
9.2 Further, to motivate the citizens for helping victims of road crashes without fear, the 
Government has notified Rule 168 and Rule 169 under the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 
1989 to protect the person, who in good faith, provide assistance to the victims of road 
crashes.  

- 11 - 
 
 9.3 The Good Samaritan Law allows a person, without expectation of payment or reward 
and without any duty of care or special relationship, voluntarily come forward to administer 
immediate assistance or emergency care to a person injured in an accident, or crash, or 
emergency medical condition. Good Samaritan Law protects Good Samaritans from 
harassment on the actions being taken by them to save the life of the road accident victims. 
9.4 MoRTH also administering a scheme for grant of Award to the Good Samaritan, who 
has saved life of a victim of an accident involving a motor vehicle by administering 
immediate assistance and rushing the victim to Hospital/Trauma Care Centre within the 
Golden Hour of the accident to provide medical treatment. The scheme provides each Good 
Samaritan with cash award of Rs. 25000/- and a certificate of appreciation per incident, 
subject to certain conditions including maximum 5 awards to an individual in a year.  
9.5 The response time for emergency services at accident sites depends on various factors 
including the traffic, weather, road condition, time, surroundings of the area etc. The 
Government has taken various initiatives for the emergency services at accident sites which 
inter-alia include: 
(i) Integrated Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) is designed with a single 
emergency number 112, to address different emergencies of citizens. 
(ii) Provision for free passage to emergency vehicles, such as an ambulance or fire service 
vehicle, etc. (Section 194E of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988). 
(iii) Protection of Good Samaritans who provide emergency medical or non-medical 
assistance to victims of motor vehicle accidents (Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 
1988). 
(iv) Provision for First-aid kit in all vehicles. (Rule 138(4) of the Central Motor Vehicles 
Rules, 1989) 
(v) Sanction of 196 Trauma Care Facilities in Government Hospitals/Medical Colleges 
across the Country under "National programme for Prevention & Management of Trauma 
and Burn injuries" by Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. 
(vi) Emergency helpline number 1033 by National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). 
(vii) Provision for Patrolling Vehicles, Ambulances, Tow-away cranes etc. in the model 
concessionaire agreement. 
(viii) Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS) is installed in high traffic density 
National Highways by NHAI. ATMS has provisions for various electronic enforcement 
devices which help in speedy identification of incidents on the highway stretches and 

- 12 - 
 
effectively monitor the highways, thereby improving the response time of the on-site 
assistance.
