The Committee is of the view that unless the Commission of Railway Safety is kept aware of the latest instructions with
 respect to railway safety issued by the Railway Board or Zonal Railways, it cannot discharge its duties effectively. 
 Ministry of Railways have admitted that copies of all important policy orders are endorsed to the Chief Commissioner
 of Railway Safety.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Railways should ensure that Commission of
 Railway Safety is on the permanent mailing list of Railway Board and Zonal Railways for all policy Circulars having
 bearing on safety and all Circulars/Orders affecting safety.  The Committee further recommends that the Commission
 of Railway Safety should be supplied with the proceeding of the Technical Committees of Railway Board so that the
 Commission remains informed of the safety problems encountered in the working of the railways and the measures
 taken to solve these problems.
(Para 67)
 
LACK OF OFFICE INFRASTRUCTURE
 
The Committee notes with concern the constraints faced by the officers of the Commission of Railway Safety in
 performing their duties due to lack of budgetary allocations and proper infrastructure and office machinery.  The
 Committee feels that the Commission of Railway Safety need adequate budgetary support from the Government so that
 it does not have to look upon the Ministry of Railways for being able to effectively discharge its duties.  The
 Committee recommends that the budget allocation of Commission of Railway Safety should be substantially increased
 so that the Commission could take care of its essential requirements such as funds for foreign training, air travel within
 India, nominations to various training courses, membership to professional institutions etc. 
(Para 69)
 
 
ANNOUNCEMENT OF PRIMA-FACIE CAUSE OF ACCIDENTS BY RAILWAY ADMINISTRATION
 
The Committee is of the opinion that the unwritten convention that no one would give the cause of an accident, when an
 enquiry is pending, needs to be followed by the Railway administration.  The Committee recommends that the Railway
 administration should refrain from speculating and giving the prime-facie cause of an accident, which is required to be
 statutorily enquired by the Commissioner of Railway Safety.  This will ensure that the credibility of the Commission of
 Railway Safety is maintained and the Commissioners are not suspected of prejudice or bias in conducting their

 enquiries.
(Para 71)
 
CONCLUSION
 
The Committee is of the opinion that the Commission of Railway Safety is an important organisation of the Government
 and, in the prevailing circumstances, the Commission's hands need strengthening in all possible ways. The Committee
 recommends that the Government should bring a comprehensive legislation incorporating the suggestion made by the
 Committee in this Report so that the functioning of the Commission of Railway Safety could improve in the interest of
 the public travelling by Indian Railways.
(Para 72)

R E P O R T
In June 2001, the erstwhile Ministry of Surface Transport was bifurcated into two Ministries viz. Ministry of

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/84threport.htm[28-08-2018 13:07:32]
 Road Transport & Highways and Ministry of Shipping.  These two Ministries have been reconstituted into one Ministry,
 viz. Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways in September 2004 with two Departments i.e. Department of
 Road Transport and Highways and Department of Shipping.
 2.         The Department of Road Transport and Highways is responsible for the formulation and implementation of
 policies relating to Road Transport and National Highways, Central Sector Road Schemes, administration of Central
 Road Fund and sponsoring of research pertaining to road works.  The two major divisions of the Department are the
 Transport Division and the Road Division.
 
3.         The Road Transport Division of the Department is concerned with the formulation of broad policies related to
 road transport besides, making arrangements for the movement of vehicular traffic with the neighboring countries. 
 
4.         The Road Division is concerned mainly with matters relating to:-
(i)                    Advising Government on all general policy matters relating to Highways
(ii)                  Development and maintenance of roads declared as National Highways
(iii)                 Development and maintenance of roads other than National Highways in   Union Territories.
(iv)                Administration of Central Road Fund (CRF) pertaining to state roads other than rural roads.
(v)                  Evaluation and specification of Standards for roads and bridges
(vi)        Research on roads. 
 5.         The following autonomous bodies function under the administrative control of the Department of Road

NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
21.       India has a vast road network of 3.32 million kilometers of which the National Highways and the State Highways
 together account for 1,95,000 km.  As on 31
st March 2004, the length of National Highways network is only 65,569 km
 constituting about 2% of the total road network in the country and carrying about 40% of the total traffic across the
 length and breadth of the country.
 
22.       The Department of Road Transport & Highways is primarily responsible for the construction and maintenance of
 National Highways (NH). All roads, other than National Highway in States, fall within the jurisdiction of respective
 state governments.  The development and maintenance of National Highways are being done on agency basis.  The
 National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), State Public Works Departments (PWDs) and the Border Road
 Organisation (BRO) are the main agencies. Out of the total National Highway length of 65,569 km, about 14,279 km
 have been entrusted to National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for improvement under National Highway
 Development Project (NHDP) Phase I & II, Port Connectivity Schemes and other schemes.  The balance lengths of
 about 46,586 km and 4,704 km of non-NHDP sections of National Highways are mainly entrusted to State PWDs and
 Border Roads Organisation (BRO) respectively, as agencies of the Ministry.

 Highways Authority of India.  The NHDP consists of Golden Quadrilateral, North-South and East-West Corridors, Port

(i)                  Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) comprising National Highways connecting four metro cities viz., Delhi,

36.       Funds for development and maintenance of National Highways are provided by the Central Government on
 yearly basis. Budgetary allocation, however, had fallen short of the requirements. In recognition of the need for funds
 for the road sector, the Union Budget for 1998-99 provided for a levy of additional excise duty and additional customs
 duty of Re.1.00 per litre of petrol. Accruals from this were made available to the National Highways Authority of India
 in 1998-99. Subsequently, an additional duty of Re.1.00 per litre on imported and domestic high speed diesel oil was
 levied from 1999-2000. In 2003-04, an additional cess of 50 paise per litre was levied on petrol and diesel. In Finance
 Minister’s budget speech for 2005-06, additional cess of 50 paise has been proposed exclusively for National
 Highways.  Revenues from these two levies are to accrue to a dedicated Central Road Fund.  This fund is a non-lapsable
 fund.  The fund has been given statutory status by the Central Road Fund Act, 2000.

NEED FOR AN INTEGRATED TRANSPORT POLICY
64.       During the meeting of the Committee held on 31
st March 2005, the Committee impressed upon the Department
 of Road Transport and Highways the need to have an integrated transport policy in the country.  The Committee pointed
 out the availability of various types of transport systems in the country and that passenger traffic was not
 proportionately distributed.  The Committee sought the opinion of the representatives of Department of Road Transport
 and Highways in the matter.  In response, while agreeing to the need to have an integrated transport policy, the
 Secretary of the Department stated as under:-
“There is definitely a need to have an integrated transport policy.  This kind of policy one has to see.  We deal
 with roads; the Shipping deals with shipping; the Civil Aviation deals with it.  One has to see it either the
 Planning Commission can do it or we can come up with an integrated transport policy for the road sector.   But,
 we are in touch with the Planning Commission on this issue.  Whatever decision is taken by the Government as a
 whole, we will abide by that.”
 65.       The Committee observes that one of the objectives for the Tenth Plan for the road sector is ‘Development of
 roads to be considered an integral part of the total transport system supplementing other modes, integrating the
 development plans with railways and other modes of transport’.   This objective of the Tenth Plan reinforces the need to
 have an integrated transport policy in the country.  The Committee is of the view that the modal-mix in terms of
 transport is very adverse in the country inspite of the fact that we have long inland waterways, a fairly large railway
 network and the recent upsurge in the aviation and road transport sector.  However, in absence of the right kind of
 modal-mix the country is not making optimum utilization of all those resources.  There is, therefore, a need to have a
 more balanced and equitable distribution of passenger and freight traffic in the country.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the Government must come forward with an integrated transport policy to make optimum utilization
 of the various transport facilities available in the country.

DAMAGE IN TSUMANI HIT AREAS
66.       The Tsunami waves hit the coastal regions of the country in December 2004 and caused a major loss of life and
 property there. The Committee desired to know from the Department of Road Transport and Highways about the
 damage caused to the road network and the relief measures undertaken by the Department in the southern parts of the
 country and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. In response, the Department of Road Transport and Highways informed the
 Committee that the Tsumani waves that hit the coastal regions of south India in December 2004 caused huge loss of life
 and property and extensive damage to road network and bridges.  Five teams of officers from the Department inspected
 the affected areas to assess the damages to road infrastructure.  About 242 km of National Highways and 520 km of
 state roads, 14 bridges and 78 culverts have been damaged in the states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and
 Union Territories of Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Pondicherry.   The total cost of repairs to damaged National
 Highways and state roads has been assessed at about Rs.200 crore (Rs.31.5 crore for short term and Rs.168.5 crore for
 long term measures).  The following relief measures were undertaken by the Department:-
A Control Room was set up by the Department which functioned from         28 th December 2004 to 28th January
 2005.  It was done with the help of all the concerned field agencies as well as other Ministries.
 
The Arasalar Bridge on NH-45A near Karaikal in the Union Territory of Pondicherry was damaged. A bailey
 bridge has been provided for immediate restoration of traffic.  A bridge by the side of the existing bridge is to be
 constructed as a permanent measure.
 
There have been extensive damages to the road network and bridges in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands also. 
 The Andaman and Nicobar Public Works Department (PWD) had requested for the supply of six power saws,
 eight generators, 20 water pumps, 6000 metre G.I. Pipes, 10 plate compactors, 100 metric tonne cement, 100
 pieces RCC Hume Pipes, 10 hand rammers, 500 metre flexible hose, 1000 metre ERW steel pipes, etc. for
 restoration works.  These items were sent by air/ship.
 
67.       The Committee was further informed that the superstructure of a 160 metre  long bridge over the Pazhyar river in
 Tamil Nadu was washed away by the tsunami waves.  The Department of Road Transport and Highways provided relief
 measures by operationalising a ferry service pending installation of a temporary steel bridge and installing a temporary
 steel bridge within 6 weeks for immediate restoration of traffic.  In addition, a permanent bridge was also proposed to be
 constructed within one and a half years.
 
68.       The Department further stated that 23 proposals amounting to Rs.80 crore had been received from the states of
 Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Union Territories of Pondicherry for restoration of the above damages.  All
 these proposals are still under examination.
 
69.       The Committee observes that the Tsunami waves caused extensive damage to the road network and bridges in the
 Southern Parts of the country.  The Committee appreciates the promptness with which the Department of Road
 Transport and Highways responded to the situation and carried out the relief measures in the tsunami hit areas.  The
 Committee strongly recommends that the Department should consider the proposals submitted by the State
 Governments for restoration of the damages on priority basis so that construction/repair works could be carried out at
 the earliest.  The Committee further observes that damage to the National Highways has badly affected the tourism
 potential in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, which is the lifeline of these islands.  The Committee recommends that

83.       The Committee understands the reasons for shortfall in respect of Pollution Testing Equipments during 2004-05. 
 Since revised emission norms have been introduced from 1.10.2004, the Committee recommends that Department of
 Road Transport and Highways should impress upon the State Governments for early procurement of pollution testing
 equipments during 2005-06 so that, if required, the allocation for the purpose could be increased at RE stage.  
 
84.       Vehicular pollution has been gaining alarming proportions in the country.  The Committee enquired from the
 Department of Road Transport and Highways regarding the steps taken by them for controlling vehicular pollution and
 monitoring pollution levels.  The Department of Road Transport and Highways apprised the Committee of some of the
 important steps taken by them to control vehicular pollution which are as under:-
·        From 1.4.2000, unleaded petrol has been made available in the country.
·        Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) have been  permitted to be used as
 alternate auto fuels.
·        India 2000 (India stage I) which are akin to Euro I norms have been made effective from 1.4.2000 throughout
 the country.
·        Bharat Stage II emission norms  which are akin to Euro II norms have already been introduced in the eleven
 mega cities and are envisaged to come into force all over India from 1.4.2005. 
·        Bharat Stage III emission standards which are akin to Euro III norms, have been notified  to come into force in
 11 mega cities from 1.4.2005.
·        The emission norms for tractors were first notified in the year 1999 and the next stage emission norms  for
 these vehicles have also come into force from 1.6.2003.  Further, even tighter emission norms for new tractors 
 are coming into force w.e.f. 1.10.2005.
·        Stricter Pollution Under Control norms have been introduced for on-road motor vehicles from 1.10.2004. 
 Apart from tighter norms for Carbon Mono Oxide (CO), the measurement of Hydro Carbon (HC) in respect of
 petrol driven vehicles have also been introduced.  Further, the testing protocol in respect of diesel vehicles has
 also been defined. States have also been empowered to prescribe tighter norms in specific areas, if there is such
 a need and the infrastructure available enables doing so.  
 
85.       The Department of Road Transport and Highways further stated that monitoring and enforcement of these norms
 for on-road vehicles comes under the purview of respective State Governments.
 
86.       The Committee is of the view that vehicular emission has become one of the major sources of environmental
 pollution and the share of the transport sector in total emissions is a matter of serious concern.  The Committee
 appreciates the steps taken by the Department of Road Transport and Highways in controlling vehicular pollution.  The
 Committee recommends that the Department of Road Transport and Highways should impress upon the State
 Governments the need for effective monitoring and enforcement of these norms for on-road vehicles so as to minimize
 its ill effects.
DIFFERENTIAL PRICING SYSTEM FOR PRIVATE VEHICLES
87.       The Committee had, in its 82
nd Report on Demands for Grants 2004-05 of the Ministry of Road Transport and
 Highways observed that the automobile population in the country had been growing disproportionately with respect to
 the infrastructure created and the roads were under undue pressure.  In view, the Committee was of the opinion that
 there was a need to adopt a policy which discourages owning of multiple vehicles.  Accordingly, the Committee had
 recommended that acquiring more than one vehicle in a family should invite financial disincentives. The Committee had
 expressed hope that this would discourage owning of multiple vehicles and  also help release the pressure on the surface
 of the roads and also help positively to reduce vehicular pollution.

 accruing to the users are not equitable. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the efforts of the Government

 should adopt a methodology, whereby, in the more densely populated states, the rich and the affluent are asked to pay

st

 functioning of the Institute.  The Committee desires that a proper enquiry may be instituted in the functioning of this
 institute.

 Development activities.  The Committee is dissatisfied that the Department of Road Transport & Highways has no
 Research & Development mechanism of its own and the Department has to depend upon other organisations for its
 Research & Development activities.  The Committee recommends that Department of Road Transport and Highways
 should develop an institutional mechanism to undertake research and development activities.  The Department should
 also create a regulator of its own with the requisite technical wherewithal for fixing emission norms, product design and
 development etc.  The Committee also recommends that the Research & Development activities should also be used for
 developing technology for creating cost-effective high quality road network such as existing in Malaysia and some other
 countries.

 promotion of use of information technology in the highway sector is one of the objectives of the Government in the
 Tenth Plan.  However, it appears that the Government has not achieved much progress in this sector especially the use
 of Information Technology in online  project monitoring system.  The Committee is of the view that Information
 Technology can also be used as an effective tool for monitoring the implementation of the projects undertaken by the
 Department.    They should also make efforts to integrate research and development activities with their monitoring
 system so that proper monitoring could be kept on the projects undertaken by them, which will also help them to keep
 tab on time overrun and cost overrun of such projects.   The Committee also recommends that efforts cited by the
 Department of Road Transport & Highways like creation of Ministry's chair in the area of development of highway
 system at Indian Institutes of Technology and creation of independent testing facilities for bridges on National
 Highways at Central Road Research Institute, New Delhi may be pursued more vigorously and in case of any difficulty,
 parallel institutions may be identified for Research & Development activities.

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE
 
ANALYSIS OF THE TENTH PLAN PROVISIONS AND ANNUAL PLAN   2005-06
            The Committee regrets to note that BE Plan Provision of Rs.7912 crore of Department of Road Transport and
 Highways was brought down to Rs.6766 crore on account of slow implementation of Externally Aided Projects by
 NHAI and the Department.  Further, there was delay in finalisation of the loans and obtaining approvals for the
 procurement for the externally aided component of the Corridor Project of NHDP (Phase-II) being financed by the
 Asian Development Bank (ADB).  Also, there was delay in award of works to the contractors and consultants for
 development of NH-34 in West Bengal.  These instances clearly bring out that on the one hand, the Department of Road
 Transport and Highways emphasizes that funds for development and maintenance of National Highways are inadequate
 while, on the other hand, the Department is not able to utilise the higher allocation made to it at BE stage.   The
 Department has failed to make optimal utilization of the funds at its disposal. The reasons for shortfall mentioned are
 delay in land acquisition, poor performance of the contractors, law and order problem etc. are very general in nature and
 are repeated every year. As a result of these, the budgetary allocations of the Department were reduced at RE stage.  The
 Committee is of the view that there is a lack of monitoring system in the Department of Road Transport and Highways.

 from December 2003 to December 2004 and now upto December 2005.  The Committee had discussed this issue in its
 82
nd Report on Demands for Grants 2004-05 of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and recommended that
 the Government should take all necessary steps to make sure that the works proposed to be completed by December
 2004 are completed within that period.  However, the Committee notes that the progress of four-laning on the Golden
 Quadrilateral project as on December 2004 was only 74%.  Thus, the steps taken by Department of Road Transport and
 Highways for timely completion of the project had not been adequate.  The Committee, therefore, would like to reiterate
 its earlier recommendation made in its 82 nd Report that the Government should take all necessary steps and evolve a
 monitoring mechanism to ensure quality of construction, making officials accountable for failure, transparency in
 implementation process, penalizing defaulting contractors etc. so that the remaining part of the project is completed by
 December 2005 and the need to further revise the target date of completion does not arise.
(Para 29)
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS NOT COVERED UNDER NHDP
            The Committee notes that in response to its recommendation for an equitable development of non-NHDP
 National Highways, the Department of Road Transport and Highways has formulated projects for development of such
 highways.  The Committee recommends that the Government should give its approval for the Accelerated North-East
 Road Development Project and NHDP Phase IV at the earliest.  Also the projects under NHDP Phase III should be
 taken up at the earliest so that the deadlines set for these projects are met.  The Committee is of the view that
 Department of Road Transport and Highways has now gained sufficient experience during the implementation of
 Golden Quadrilateral.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that Department of Road Transport and Highways
 should adopt a proactive approach and take care that the hindrances resulting in delay in timely completion of such

 implementation of the projects and the deadlines set for the project are met unlike the Golden Quadrilateral where the
 target date of completion has gone up by two years so far.

            The Committee takes exception to the fact that funds accruing to the Central Road Fund due to levy of additional
 cess since 1.4.2003 have not been provided to the Department of Road Transport and Highways, inspite of the fact that
 this additional cess of 50 paise per litre on petrol and diesel was levied primarily to support the implementation of
 National Highway Development Project (NHDP).  There has been no positive outcome to this impasse inspite of a
 direction by the Cabinet for implementation of the recommendations of the Group of Ministers.  The Committee
 recommends that the Department of Road Transport and Highways should take up the matter with the Ministry of
 Finance  so that the funds due to the Department are provided to it at the earliest and the projects under National
 Highway Development Project do not suffer for want of funds.

            One of the objectives of the Tenth Plan for Road Sector is special attention to the development of roads in North-
Eastern region.  Although three years of the Five Year Plan have gone by, the Government has not taken any concrete
 steps for improving the National Highways network in this region.  Also, the Special Accelerated Road Development
 Programme in the North-Eastern region is still under consideration of the Government. The Committee feels that
 development of road network is very crucial in the context of the development of North-Eastern region of the country.

PARTICIPATION OF PRIVATE SECTOR IN DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF NATIONAL
 HIGHWAYS
            The Committee feels that in view of the huge resource gap of around Rs.1,06,000 crore in the road sector during
 the Tenth Plan, there is a genuine need to attract private sector investment in this sector to a large extent.  However, the
 Government has not been able to attract private sector investment to the desired extent.  The Committee recommends
 that the Government should project the success of the Golden Quadrilateral to the private sector to encourage them to
 contribute more and more to the development of this sector.  This would definitely help the Government to reduce the
 resource gap position to a large extent.

 North-Eastern region of the country to the extent required by them.  The Committee recommends that, in such a
 scenario, keeping in view the socio-economic conditions of the North-Eastern region, the Government must provide
 resources for the projects on its own and the developmental activities in road sector for North-Eastern region should not
 be allowed to be a casualty.

NEED FOR AN INTEGRATED TRANSPORT POLICY
            The Committee observes that one of the objectives for the Tenth Plan for the road sector is ‘Development of
 roads to be considered an integral part of the total transport system supplementing other modes, integrating the
 development plans with railways and other modes of transport’.   This objective of the Tenth Plan reinforces the need to
 have an integrated transport policy in the country.  The Committee is of the view that the modal-mix in terms of
 transport is very adverse in the country inspite of the fact that we have long inland waterways, a fairly large railway
 network and the recent upsurge in the aviation and road transport sector.  However, in absence of the right kind of
 modal-mix the country is not making optimum utilization of all those resources.  There is, therefore, a need to have a
 more balanced and equitable distribution of passenger and freight traffic in the country.  The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that the Government must come forward with an integrated transport policy to make optimum utilization
 of the various transport facilities available in the country.

 Department of Road Transport and Highways is concerned, the working in different parts of the country is affected due

                                                                              R E P O R T
 
India has one of the most ancient civilization and cultural heritage. In the cultural continuum, different communities through their creative expressions and belief pattern contributed

 significantly over centuries which well blended in the mainstream gradually. This unity in diversity is a distinctive characteristic of Indian culture.  Therefore, in a pluralist social mosaic
 culture is the most crucial role-player which gives meaning to our present existence. The role of Culture lies not only in the context of promotion of economic growth but also in relation to
 other objectives of creating an environment that encourages self-expression and exploration on the part of individuals and communities besides support to arts and artists and encouraging
 active participation in cultural expression by people at large, and developing creativity as a social force.
2.         The Ministry of Culture, which was set up in 1985 through the 174 th Amendment of the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 was part of the Ministry of
 Human Resource Development; later it was transferred to the newly created Ministry of Tourism and Culture. In May 2004 it has been declared as an independent Ministry and is now
 Ministry of Culture. The Ministry is responsible for the promotion, preservation and conservation of the tangible and intangible cultural heritage of the country. It also promotes mutual
 understanding, goodwill and foster closer relations with foreign countries. Preservation of ancient and historic monuments and records, exploration and excavation of archaeological sites
 and remains, maintenance and expansion of libraries and museums of national importance and observance of centenaries and anniversaries of eminent personalities are among its other
 responsibilities. The institutions of the Ministry, which are engaged in promotion, and dissemination of art and culture broadly are the Zonal  Cultural Centers, Center for Cultural Resources
 and Training, and through the Schemes operated Departmentally. The public private participation in the Ministry is done under the aegis of the National Culture Fund.
3.         The programmes undertaken by the Ministry of Culture can broadly be classified as, Activities of North East Region, Archaeology, Museums, Anthropology and Ethnology,
 Archives and Archival Libraries, Tibetan/Buddhist Studies, Libraries, Akademies and National School of Drama, Promotion and Dissemination of Culture, Memorials, Centenaries and
 Anniversaries, Cultural Relations and Festival of India, IGNCA and Secretariat.
4.         Plan programmes of the Ministry of Culture relating to promotion, preservation and conservation of the cultural heritage of the country is implemented through a network of 2
 attached offices, 6 subordinate offices and 26 Autonomous organisations under its control and through 16 schemes directly operated by the Ministry for promotion and dissemination of art
 and culture.  Its activities and programmes have been organized under eleven broad heads. They are Promotion & Dissemination, Archaeology, Museums, Archives, Anthropology,
 Performing Arts, Libraries, Buddhist and Tibetan Institutes, Activities for North Eastern Region and Other Expenditure.

8.         Demand No.20 containing the details of budget allocation of the Ministry of Culture for the financial year 2005-06 was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing
 Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 29
th March 2005.  The Secretary Ministry of Culture during the course of oral evidence held on 29 th March 2005,
 deposed before the Committee :
“This year has been a difficult year for them as the Ministry had major financial constraints.  The budget was passed late and they had accordingly a shorter time to spend the
 money allocated to them.  There was also a cap by the Ministry of Finance.   Accordingly the Ministry of Culture had to spend 65% of the money by December and thereafter
 there was a slash of about Rs.65 crore at the revised budget stage.  After intervention of the Ministry they got restoration of the cut to the extent of Rs.20 crore.  But this has
 certainly put a strain on the institutions/field offices functioning under the Ministry.”
 
9.         The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Culture had proposed an outlay of Rs.551.12 crore and also got an approved outlay of the same amount with a capital component
 of Rs.61.80 crore.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Culture will be able to utilize the funds for implementation of new Schemes/Projects optimally. 
10.       The Committee, however, is not convinced about the reasons cited by the Ministry that budget was passed late and accordingly, there was shorter time available to spend the money
 allocated to them and observes that if the annual plan starts after the beginning of the financial year itself, then it considerably reduces the capacity of the Ministry to plan out expenditure.  
 Therefore, the planning for financial progress has to start even before as the broad heads are already known to the Ministry under the contours of the five-year plan.  The Committee also
 fails to understand as to how this intra-year financial development should deter the Ministry in planning it in such a manner that none of the financial allocations made can be successfully
 used by the end of the year.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Finance Ministry recalling the money which has been already allocated is a serious problem and the
 Ministry should take adequate care and evolve a sound method of financial planning so that such kind of circumstance may never occur in future.

11.       The Committee further enquired about the impact of the new budgetary provisions on the various activities of the Ministry of Culture with details in respect of which plan outlays
 were reduced by the Ministry of Finance or the Ministry of Culture could not utilise the allocated funds.  To this the Ministry informed the Committee that under the new budget, the major
 institutions under the Ministry, like the ASI, Museums, Science  Cities, ZCCs and  Akademies, etc. have received enhanced allocation.  This will help them to take up new projects and
 address major issues like upgradation, conservation, security, dissemination, digitization etc.  Besides, the various grant-in-aid schemes implemented by the Ministry will also have better
 allocation so as to entertain larger number of applicants.
12.       The Committee noted that in the Expenditure Budget (2005-06) the Ministry of Culture has got budgetary sanction of Rs.126.98 crores under the head ‘Others’ (Art & Culture),
 which was just Rs.59.15 in the RE 2004-05.  Accordingly, the Ministry was requested to as to how they would absorb this enhanced allocation.  The Ministry informed the Committee that
 the head ‘Others’ (Art & Culture), includes the Organizations/ Schemes namely, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Gandhi Smriti  and Darshan Samiti, Maulana Abdul Kalam
 Azad Institute of Asian Studies, Kolkata, Kalakshetra Foundation, Chennai, Fellowships to outstanding artists, Financial assistance to Himalayan Arts, Financial Assistance for
 Buddhist/Tibetan institutes, setting up of Multi Purpose Complexes (MPCC), Assistance to cultural organisation (R.K Mission Institute of Culture Kolkata ), Development of cultural
 organisations etc. In view of drastic cut of Rs.67 crore at RE stage, it was decided to provide original budget allocation i.e. BE. 2004-05 level with a marginal step up of provision for
 augmenting the activities of these organisations and of schemes during the year 2005-06. Besides, Rs.6.00 crore allocation to the scheme of setting up of MPCC was made in addition to last
 year’s budget of Rs. 9.00 crore. The additional amount provided would be spent on setting up of new Multi Proposes Cultural Complexes in Manipur, Nagaland , Assam, Rajasthan,
 Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh.  As per the instructions of the Ministry of Finance, an additional amount of Rs. 46 crore has been provided for the first time under the Plan Scheme of
 Centenaries and Anniversaries Celebrations during 2005-06. This provision is kept in fact for the project on Khalsa Heritage Memorial Complex, Anandpur Sahib. Hon’ble Prime Minister
 during his visit to Amritsar has announced that the Government would provide necessary financial assistance for the purpose.
13.       The Committee notes that the Ministry of Culture this time has given more emphasis to various reputed institutes of art and culture like, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies,
 Gandhi Smriti and Darshan Samiti, Buddhist and Tibetan Institutes, Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes, Ram Krishna Mission Institute of Culture, Kolkata, etc.  The Committee hopes that
 the construction of proposed new Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes in Manipur, Nagaland, Assam, Rajasthan, Chattisgarh  and Andhra Pradesh would be completed in time.  The
 Committee further directs that the additional amount of Rs.46 crore which has been for the first time provided for Centenaries and Anniversaries Celebration will be spent fairly and in an
 unbiased manner. The Committee also recommends that ongoing projects on publication of volumes of works of Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan be completed in time and funds for that
 purpose will be provided as assured by the Ministry.    Moreover, Birth Anniversary Celebrations of Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan and Choudhary Charan Singh should be continued
 every year.  The Committee strongly recommends that the entire provisions made by the Ministry of Culture be utilised during the year 2005-06.  
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA
 14.      The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was established in 1861.  It is an attached office of the Ministry of Culture.  Since its establishment, 144 years ago, the ASI has grown into
 a large organization having its network throughout the country.  At present, the ASI has declared 3656 monuments, which are of national importance in the country, including 17 properties
 inscribed on the World Heritage List by UNESCO.  The major activities of the ASI are maintenance, conservation and preservation of centrally protected monuments/sites and remains.  It
 conducts archeological exploration and excavation regularly.  It also keeps developing epigraphical research, setting up and reorganization of site museums and training in archaeology. The
 Archaeological Survey of India has prepared perspective plans for the 10
th Five Year Plan period which envisaged an integrated approach covering conservation, preservation, landscaping,
 organizing/ re-organising of site museums and problem oriented excavations and exploration.   With a holistic approach, the Archaeological Survey of India is devoted towards creation of
 cultural hubs encompassing facilities for domestic and foreign tourists.  The proposed cultural hubs are, i.e. Mahabalipuram, Ajanta & Ellora , Hampi, Kurukshetra, Chittorgarh,
 Kumbhalgarh, Sibsagar monuments and   Fatehpur Sikri.
15.       Plan allocation to the Archaeological Survey of India has increased by Rs.10 crore in the BE 2005-06 in comparison to BE 2004-05 of Rs.70.00 crores which was reduced to
 Rs.58.00 crores in the RE stage.  The Committee desired to know the reasons for increasing the fund under this head.  The Ministry has replied that the original budget allocation under Plan
 during the year 2004-05 was Rs.70.00 Crores.  Subsequently Ministry of Culture has reduced the Plan budget allocation to Archaeological Survey of India for 2004-05 to Rs.48.00 Crores. 
 Anticipating that as this drastic cut would affect the conservation and other archaeological works of the ASI, ASI requested to reconsider the reduction in budget allocation to ASI.  Taking
 into consideration the above, the Ministry of Culture partially restored the budget allocation (Plan), under R.E. for 2004-05 to Rs.58.00 Crores.  Ministry of Culture has conveyed that
 Rs.80.00 Crores has been allocated to ASI for the financial year 2005-06.  The allocation has been increased with a view to give special focus on management plan of the World Heritage
 Sites and special focus on strengthening of selected site museums.
16.       The Committee desired to know the details of projects works to be undertaken by ASI during the year 2005-06.  To this the Ministry replied that all appurtenant lands adjoining the
 protected monuments, which are also a part of the protected area, are being surveyed and fenced to develop as greens. Linkages are being developed between the Ministry of Culture and the
 Department of Tourism in order to ensure that growth in a particular cluster of monuments is integrated.Greater  thrust is being given to collaborations with the Corporate Sector such as the
 Taj Group of Hotels World Monuments Fund etc. for formulation of Master Plans and for implementation of integrated development of some important monuments.  ASI has taken-up a

(iii)       Problem of Encroachment and Security of Monuments/Sites under the Protection of ASI:
 
28.       The Committee was quite concerned about the illegal encroachment of monuments/sites under the protection of ASI and desired to know from the Ministry as to what was being done
 to check the encroachment around the monuments.  The Ministry of Culture replied that as and when an encroachment is noticed in the protected area of a monument, the Superintending
 Archaeologist issues a notice to the encroacher as per the provisions of the Ancient  Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.  A complaint is also lodged with the local
 police.  When no response is received from the encroacher, the DG, ASI issues a notice ordering the illegal occupant to vacate the occupied site and remove the encroachment.  If no action
 is taken by the encroacher, the DG, ASI issues an order under Section 19 (2) of the Ancient  Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 and Rule 38 (2) of the Ancient
 Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Rules, 1959 to the Collector and the concerned district authorities for demolition and removal of the encroachment.  The Archaeological
 Survey of India also initiates legal action in the courts against the encroachers.  Though the Superintending Archaeologists have been vested with the power of Estate Officer and authorized
 to issue eviction notices under the Public Premises Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants (Act), 1971, the successful removal of encroachment depends upon  entirely on the cooperation of
 the police and district authorities, which is seldom forthcoming.   In the Delhi Circle specifically, there are encroachments on 14 centrally protected monuments and action is under way for
 their removal.  In the case of several encroachments, the matter is sub-judice in the courts of law.  In so far as the Siri Fort Wall is concerned, the protected  stretch of the fortification wall is
 free from encroachment, but a portion of the Siri Fort Wall, which is not under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India and falling within Shahpur Jat Village, is encroached
 upon by the villagers.   There are two cases in the Court in respect of Siri Fort Wall.
29.       The Director-General, ASI during the course of oral evidence also submitted that  :
"Encroachment in and around ASI monuments is one of the problems ASI is facing.  3,658 monuments are protected.  If you put a reasonable number of people to protect it, it
 would require at least 7-8 thousand people.  If you take monuments like the Taj or Red Fort, each would take at least 200 people.  In fact, it is consuming one-third of the
 staff to protect just these two.  There is no physical protection at all and the encroachment is going on for several years.  We have powers to issue notice for the people to
 vacate.  But we don't have the power to compel them to vacate. This State Government police support hardly ever comes." 
 
30.       The Ministry of Culture informed the Committee that at present, there are 3463 Monument Attendants in Archaeological Survey of India.  CISF personal have been employed in Red
 Fort in Delhi and the Taj Mahal in Agra.  For 459 CISF personnel employed in these two sensitive monuments, the financial implication per year is Rs.9.25 crores.  Besides, 100 State
 Police personnel are being paid for deployment at some monuments and museums.  The total payment involved to the State Police personnel is Rs.1.5 crores annually.  However a large
 number of protected monuments all over the country are not having any security.  There is no precise estimate of the funds required for providing security guards to all these monuments. 
 However on purely tentative estimates, it is estimated that an amount of Rs.100 crores may be required annually for proper physical security to all the protected monuments by way of
 deploying private security guards.
31.       The Committee expresses its anxiety over the incidents of encroachment upon the land of Centrally Protected Monuments.  The Committee is more concerned about the inability of
 Archeological Survey of India to get back the land from encroachers.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that a complete assessment should be made regarding encroachment
 of monuments/sites under the protection of Archaeological Survey of India all over the country.  Prompt action ought be taken against the encroachers with the help of State
 Governments/Local Administrations and the matter should be pursued at the highest level.  The Committee also recommends that adequate budgetary provisions should be made for security

INDIRA GANDHI NATIONAL CENTRE FOR THE ARTS
60.       Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) is a premier national institution engaged in the pursuit of knowledge on arts and culture and in the exploration of relationships of
 arts and culture with various disciplines of learning and diverse aspects of life.  Established in 1985 in the memory of the Late Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi, it has multifarious
 activities such as research, publication, training, documentation, dissemination and networking and is poised to grow into a large repository of information pertaining to the arts in India. 
 The IGNCA seeks to place the arts within the natural and human environment by providing a forum for creative and critical dialogue between the diverse arts, between the arts and sciences,
 between the arts and the traditional and current knowledge systems.   The IGNCA promotes interaction and understanding between diverse communities, regions, social strata, and between
 India and other parts of the world.

 (2004-05) it was Rs.40.00 lakh.

 Ministry of Culture informed that with reference to the setting up of the National Mission for Preservation of India’s  Intangible Cultural Heritage, comments were received from the

75.       The Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCC) were created to promote cultural awareness and to identify, nurture and promote vanishing folk art traditions in the rural and semi urban areas.

 Centre functions as an autonomous body, with the Governor of the State, where it is located serving as the ex officio  Chairman.  In Budget Estimate 2005-06 an amount of Rs.30 crore has
 been allocated to the Zonal Cultural Centres as against of Rs.19 crore allocated in RE 2004-05. The main source of income for meeting administrative expenditure of the ZCCs is the
 interest accrued on the  fixed deposits of the corpus fund.  The falling interest rate has resulted in the reduction of income from the corpus fund while expenditure on establishment costs
 have increased due to inflation, increase in artists remuneration, increase in salary etc.   To tide over the financial crises an allocation of Rs.35 crores was provided in 10
th Five Year Plan i.e.
 Rs.5 crores per ZCC for corpus fund.

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS 
 AT A GLANCE
 
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry of Culture had proposed an outlay of Rs.551.12 crore and also got an approved outlay of the same amount with a capital component
 of Rs.61.80 crore.   The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Culture will be able to utilize the funds for implementation of new Schemes/Projects optimally. 
            The Committee, however, is not convinced about the reasons cited by the Ministry that budget was passed late and accordingly, there was shorter time available to spend the money
 allocated to them and observes that if the annual plan starts after the beginning of the financial year itself, then it considerably reduces the capacity of the Ministry to plan out expenditure.  
 Therefore, the planning for financial progress has to start even before as the broad heads are already known to the Ministry under the contours of the five-year plan.  The Committee also
 fails to understand as to how this intra-year financial development should deter the Ministry in planning it in such a manner that none of the financial allocations made can be successfully
 used by the end of the year.  Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Finance Ministry recalling the money which has been already allocated is a serious problem and the
 Ministry should take adequate care and evolve a sound method of financial planning so that such kind of circumstance may never occur in future.
            The Committee notes that the Ministry of Culture this time has given more emphasis to various reputed institutes of art and culture like, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies,
 Gandhi Smriti and Darshan Samiti, Buddhist and Tibetan Institutes, Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes, Ram Krishna Mission Institute of Culture, Kolkata, etc.  The Committee hopes that
 the construction of proposed new Multi Purpose Cultural Complexes in Manipur, Nagaland, Assam, Rajasthan, Chattisgarh  and Andhra Pradesh would be completed in time.  The
 Committee further directs that the additional amount of Rs.46 crore which has been for the first time provided for Centenaries and Anniversaries Celebration will be spent fairly and in an
 unbiased manner. The Committee also recommends that ongoing projects on publication of volumes of works of Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan be completed in time and funds for that
 purpose will be provided as assured by the Ministry.    Moreover, Birth Anniversary Celebrations of Lok Nayak Jaiprakash Narayan and Choudhary Charan Singh should be continued
 every year.  The Committee strongly recommends that the entire provisions made by the Ministry of Culture be utilised during the year 2005-06.

st report of Demands for Grants (2004-05) of Ministry of Shipping which reads as under:-
"The Committee fails to understand as to how the physical targets will be achieved with this low utilization pattern.  In fact, the Committee feels that this raises doubts about

21.    When enquired about the details of encouraging private sector participation and framing of guidelines for involvement of private sector for development of infrastructure services in
 the port sector, the Department of Shipping informed that the existing policy dispensation provides for private sector participation including foreign direct investment upto 100% in the
 port sector. The Government's endeavour is to provide a facilitative investor friendly environment with transparent procedures and decision making process for encouraging private sector
 participation in the sector.  The Government has, issued comprehensive guidelines for attracting private sector participation in major ports as also for formation of joint ventures by major
 ports for development of infrastructure services. The guidelines preferred route for private sector participation through open competitive bidding in which the bidder offering the highest
 percentage of revenue share out of the operation of the facility is selected.  Tariff Authority for Major ports (TAMP) which is an independent statutory authority fixes the tariffs to be
 charged from the port users by the private operators. These tariffs act as a ceiling and the private operators are free to charge below these ceilings.
 
22.    The major ports can also form joint ventures with publicly owned foreign ports for attracting new technology, introducing better managerial practices, etc.  In case it is considered
 that certain technology, expertise, managerial practices are necessary to be imported from a particular country, Government to Government arrangements for formation of a joint venture
 between a major port in India and a foreign port to be selected by the foreign Government can also be considered.  These joint ventures can be formed without following the tender route. 
 The form of collaboration will be on BOT basis. 
 
23.    In the reply to a query regarding achievement in attracting private sector participation in major ports, the Department of Shipping informed that at present, 37 private sector/captive
 port projects involving capacity addition of about 137 MTPA and an investment of about Rs.9756 crore are at various stage of evaluation and implementation. Out of these 13 Projects
 with capacity addition of about 47.40 MTPA involving an investment of about Rs.2597 crore have been operationalised.  However, the focus during the Annual Plan 2005-06 and Tenth
 Five Year Plan period will continue to be on the following:-

 depending on the draft required, moving between east and west coast of India could have a continuous navigable sea route around the Peninsula within India's own territorial waters.  This

 facilities especially in the design of vessels and night navigation facilities and identification of economical viable routes for the development of IWT sector in the country, the Department
 of Shipping apprised the Committee that admittedly there is a need to strengthen R&D facilities especially in the design of vessels, night navigation facilities and identification of
 economically viable routes. Good progress has been made since last year in installing night navigation facilities in all 3 national waterways. For night navigation facilities, a system of
 buoys and lights is being installed in NW-3.  Earlier in NW-1 and 2 also, buoys with light were tried but due to large water level fluctuation and high current velocity these were
 unsuccessful. In NW-1 and 2, therefore, system of deploying manned country boats fitted with lights atop has been implemented in Tribeni- Farakka sector (NW-1) and Dhubri-Guwahati
 sector (NW-2), and it has been found successful.  As regards design of vessels, IWAI is being assisted by NSDRC.   Further, identification of economically viable routes has been got done
 through M/s. IFCI Ltd. in the context of Private Sector participation.
 
108.     The Committee notes with dismay that Research & Development Studies facilities especially in design of vessels and night navigation facilities and identification of economically
 viable routes for development of Inland Water Transport sector has not been given due consideration.  The Committee is of the view that Research & Development activities is the
 backbone for success of any sector and recommends the Department of Shipping to strengthen the Research & Development facilities for development of Inland Water Transport Sector in
 the country.
 
109.     As regards, linking the investment in IWT sector with achievement of physical targets for cargo transportation. The Department of Shipping informed that Indian Institute of
 Management, Calcutta has been appointed by IWAI for undertaking the study on the following lines:-                      
(i)                  Collection of data relating to movement of cargo and passengers in NWs 1,2 & 3 for both organized and unorganized sector.
(ii)                Identification of water stretches where IWT operations are happening at present and infrastructure presently available at points of IWT operations. Preparation of list of
 inland waterways operators who would be interested in movement of cargo through IWT mode.
(iii)               Preparation of list of potential commodities (with O-Ds), which could be, transported through NWs 1,2 & 3 indicating quantities of commodities. Indicate realistic
 targets (tones-km. and Rs.in crores) for movement of cargo in all three NWs by end of 10
th, 11th and 12th plans. The report of the consultant is expected by May 2005.
 
110.     The Committee is happy to note that Department of Shipping has appointed a consultant for working out a realistic target for cargo transportation vis-à-vis targeted investments for
 Inland Water Transport promotion for the 10th Plan and beyond as per its recommendation.  The Committee hopes that the study for linking the investment in Inland Water Transport
 sector with achievement of physical targets for cargo transportation will certainly enhance the prospects of Inland Water Transport and help to boost the growth of cargo traffic in Inland
 Water Transport sector. The Committee directs the Department of Shipping to apprise it about the progress in the matter.

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
AT A GLANCE
 
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06
            The Committee expresses its concern over the failure of Department of Shipping to spend the approved outlay.  During the year 2004-05, out of the budgeted amount of Rs.2419.66
 crore the Department could spent only Rs.1400.99 crore which clearly indicates the poor fiscal management in the Department of Shipping.  The Committee observes that even while
 revising allocations, little consideration has been paid to the actual expenditure incurred in the past.  This shows that budgetary and revised estimates have always been made without
 taking into account the actual requirements as experienced in the previous years.
           
The Committee feels that Department of Shipping has not evolved effective system or planning to systematically anticipate, assess and project its actual requirements of funds
 otherwise the investments could have yielded commensurate returns.  The Committee recommends that in future, the Department of Shipping should be transparent and realistic while
 making projections of required funds so that resources may not remain unused and are allocated more judiciously.

(Paras 10 & 11)
PORT SECTOR
The Committee is unhappy with the poor performance of Department of Shipping with regard to under utilization of approved outlays over the years for the port sector.  During the
 Financial year 2004-05, an outlay of Rs.1066.55 crore was allocated for the port sector but the ports could utilize only Rs.440.51 crore. The Committee is dismayed by this repeated failure
 of Department of Shipping and is surprised as to why the Ministry asks for so much of allocation if it is not in position to spend the approved outlay. The Committee desires that the
 Department of Shipping should take all corrective measures based upon actual requirements for maximum utilization of budgeted amount during 2005-06.  In this regard, the Committee
 reiterates its earlier recommendation contained in 81st report of Demands for Grants (2004-05) of Ministry of Shipping which reads as under:-
"The Committee fails to understand as to how the physical targets will be achieved with this low utilization pattern.  In fact, the Committee feels that this raises doubts about
 the mismatch in the projections for physical and financial targets.  The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Shipping has full responsibility to ensure proper
 utilization of the approved outlay.  The Committee feels that strict monitoring is crucial for timely completion of any project.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that
 the monitoring agency should play rather proactive role and do away with the procedural hurdles for timely completion of the projects so that the budgeted allocation is
 utilized optimally.  The Committee also recommends the Ministry to keep informed about the progress in the matter."
            (Para 16)
CAPACITY AND TRAFFIC IN MAJOR PORT
            The Committee expresses its appreciation for achievement of the capacity of major ports which has either exceeded the target or likely to achieve target fixed for cargo handling of
 all commodities except container.  The containerization is the emerging global trend in the mode of cargo trade in which the country is lagging behind which is a matter of concern.
           
The Committee feels that a proper environment with transparent procedures and decision making process can give boost to private sector participation in the port sector.  The
 Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to review the existing guidelines on Private Sector Participation in the port sector with emphasis on overcoming capital
 constraints, technology upgradation and value addition.
(Paras 26 & 27)
TONNAGE TAX
            The Committee notes that the Government has since introduced the tonnage tax regime to the dredgers also as per its recommendation.  The Committee feels that introduction of
 tonnage tax in lieu of corporate tax will not only facilitate investment in shipping sector but also provide a level playing field to the Indian Shipping Industry vis-à-vis its foreign
 counterparts and the shipping companies will be able to acquire more tonnage.  However, the Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for excluding the vessels registered under
 the Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian coastal vessel Act, 1838.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matter for extending the benefits of tonnage tax to the vessels registered
 under Indian Vessels Act 1917 and Indian Coastal Vessels Act, 1838 may be pursued further with the Ministry of Finance as this also vitally linked to the viability of the Inland Water
 Transport sector.
(Para 31)
SETHUSAMUDRAM SHIP CHANNEL PROJECT
            The Committee notes the Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project is of great economic and strategic importance which will connect the Gulf of Mannar to Bay of Bengal so that the
 ship moving between East and West coast of India could have a continuous navigable sea route within their own territorial waters and the proposed channel save upto 424 nautical miles of
 travel and about 30 hours of sailing time for ships.  The Committee notes with satisfaction that Ministry of Environment & Forests has also given environmental clearance to the project
 and a special purpose vehicle has been incorporated to raise finance to create and operate navigable channel.  The Committee expects that the project once completed will serve the
 strategic and national security interests besides spuring the overall economic development of coastal districts of southern states.  The Committee however, recommends that while taking
 up the implementation of the project, the Department of Shipping must give due attention to the likely effect of natural calamities particularly one like as Tsunami which hit southern
 states during December 2004 and safety measures may be incorporated accordingly.
  (Para 36)
CRUISE SHIPPING
            The Committee is of the view that sea travel is becoming increasingly popular and there is enormous potential for its growth and expansion in India.  The Committee notes that six
 major ports- Mumbai, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Kochi, Tuticorin and Chennai have been identified for the development of infrastructure and other facilities with a view to make India
 an attractive cruise destination.  The Committee notes that a High Power Steering Group has been set up with a view to catalyze the growth and development of cruise shipping and to
 remove bottlenecks and a policy is being formulated in the regard. The Committee hopes that the group will submit its report expeditiously and the policy is framed at the earliest so that
 the benefit of opportunity available to cruise tourism sector is exploited.  The Committee recommends that pending finalization of policy, the Department of Shipping must take steps to
 attract investments from private sector with a view to create infrastructure and other facilities for development of cruise shipping especially in ports on the Eastern parts of the country
 including Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshdweep Islands having great potential in that area.
(Para 40)
CALCUTTA  DOCK LABOUR BOARD
            The Committee is distressed to note that the employees of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board are not being treated as Government employees so far as payment of pension and
 pensionary benefits are concerned, though, the Calcutta Dock Labour Board, a body corporate, was constituted in terms of section 5(A) of the Dock Workers (Regulation of Employment)
 Act, 1948 in September 1952.  The Committee expresses its concern that inspite of specific provisions under the Act, the rules and regulations concerning pension for employees of
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board have not been approved by Department of Expenditure and the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board are being made victims under the cover that
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board constitutes an autonomous body and therefore, denied of the benefits for long.

            The Committee is of the firm opinion that liabilities on account of payment of arrears of pensions and pensionary dues of Calcutta Dock Labour Board entirely lies on the
 Government and the Government cannot be absolved of its liability and withhold pension and post retirement benefits to the employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board on one pretext or
 other.  The Committee, strongly recommends, the Department of Shipping to vigorously pursue the matter with Ministry of Finance for release of enhanced grant to Calcutta Dock Labour
 Board for meeting its pensionary liabilities and implement comprehensive restructuring of Calcutta Dock Labour Board for introduction of Voluntary Retirement Scheme.
 
            The Committee is of the view that problem for payment of pension and pensionary dues can be resolved once and for all, if the Government approves self-sustaining proposal for
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board's pensioners with provisions for an initial corpus and an appropriate policy and methodology for payment of pension worked out for the future.  The
 Committee, therefore reiterates, that the Government should build a corpus of pension fund for discharging the future pensionary liabilities of the Board, as the bulk of its employees will
 retire in another two years.
(Paras 49, 50 &51)
MISAPPROPRIATION OF SEAMEN'S PROVIDENT FUND
            The Committee is deeply concerned that the shortage to the tune of Rs.92.78 crore in Seamen's Provident Fund, which lost due to security scam, has not yet been recouped by the
 Department of Shipping.  The Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for delay in recouping the fund, which is entirely managed by the Government and feels that any further
 delay may cause adverse impact in protection of interests of the seamen's whose life long savings stands jeopardized in the scam.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department
 of Shipping to approach the Ministry of Finance for grants-in-aid to recoup the shortage in the Seamen's Provident Fund.
 
            The Committee further recommends that in order to ensure that such happenings are not repeated in future, sufficient legislative and administrative safeguards have to be built in the
 system.  At the same time, those responsible for such scam should not be spared and suitable action including criminal action ought to be taken against them so that such actions provide
 deterrence to other as well.  The Committee would like to be apprised of the action in this regard.
(Paras 55 & 56)
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF MARITIME STUDIES (IIMS)
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Department of Shipping is in the process of drafting Indian Maritime University Bill for the establishment of Indian Maritime
 University under an Act of Parliament and a token provision has been made by the Government for development of Indian Maritime  University. The Committee feels that the move will
 certainly give boost to quality education in the field of marine training.  However, the Committee is unhappy to note that no definite time limit has been fixed for establishment of Indian
 Maritime University and recommends, the Department of Shipping to fix definite time frame for the establishment of Indian Maritime University under a Central Act.  The Committee
 further hopes that while finalizing the location of the Indian Maritime University, existing infrastructure and assests have to be taken into cognizance. 
           
The Committee hopes that the issues pertaining to creation of pension fund and finalization of terms & condition for the absorption of employees of Indian Institute of Maritime
 Studies will be taken care of by the Department without any disadvantage to the employees in the draft bill itself and recommends the Department of Shipping to apprise the Committee of
 the development in this regard.
(Paras 62 & 63)
HINDUSTAN SHIPYARD LIMITED
            The Committee takes note of the fact that Hindustan Shipyard Limited is changing its marketing strategy by engaging itself in the utilization of installed capacity for increasing
 ship-repair turnover.  The vigorous marketing efforts are showing results  and Hindustan Shipyard Limited has been able to secure the hi-tech, hi-value repair orders for betterment of the
 financial health of the yard.  The Committee appreciates the decision of the Government for rehabilitation of Hindustan Shipyard Limited by way of financial restructuring for improving
 the performance of the yard and recommends for expeditious clearance of the proposal for the capital restructuring of the Hindustan Shipyard Limited.                                     
(Para 76)
HOOGHLY DOCK & PORT ENGINEERS LIMITED
            The Committee is happy to note that a rehabilitation-cum-revival package has been prepared for Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited and a token provision has also been kept
 for the purpose as per its recommendation.  The Committee is of the opinion that Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited with its infrastructure and a expertise can be a integral part for
 development and promotion of Inland Water Transport through NW-1 and NW-2 and contribute to the national economy as well. The Committee, therefore recommends the Government
 to grant clearance for the revival package of Hooghly Dock & Port Engineers Limited expeditiously.
(Para 82)
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
The Committee notes with distress that the matter for disinvestments of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd has been referred to the Board for Reconstruction of Public
 Sector Enterprises.  The Committee feels that the Government has not made much efforts to improve the financial health of the company.  The Committee is gravely concern by the fact
 that inspite of repeated recommendation in the past the Government has not yet been able to come out with a complete blueprint for making full use of the existing assets of the company
 in ensuring productive potential by exploring all possibilities like merger with similar entities and integration with Inland Water Transport. The Committee is firmly of the view that the
 future of Inland Water Transport operations including that of Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd holds immense possibilities for establishing a well-defined multimodal
 transportation network in the country and therefore recommends the Department of Shipping to take steps to improve the performance of the Central Inland Water Transport Corporation
 Ltd besides impressing upon the Ministry of Finance for capital restructuring with its existing infrastructure, capacity and manpower.
(Para 91)
INLAND WATER TRANSPORT

 and merely accounts for 0.15% of cargo movement in the country.  The Committee observes that though measures to boost the growth of cargo traffic have been put in place and
 department is committed to raise the share of Inland Water Transport to 2% over the next 8-20 years. The Committee however, notes that with a view to compete with the other developed
 modes of transport, the Department of Shipping is working on declaration and development of three more waterways as National Waterways and a task force to monitor the progress of
 Inland Water Transport projects has also been formed. The Committee, recommends the Department of Shipping to exploit the full potential of this efficient mode of transport, besides,
 addressing the issues of development of adequate infrastructure facilities namely fairways, terminal and navigational aids on the existing three NWs.
 
            The Committee also recommends the Government to improve the modal-mix of transport in the country and prepare a road map for integrated transport policy to include   Inland
 Water Transport, Coastal Shipping, Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways and Railways.
            The Committee is perturbed to note the practice of under utilization of budgeted amount by the Department of Shipping over the years.  During 2004-05, the Department of
 Shipping has projected Rs.133.50 crore plan outlays for Inland Water Transport sector, which was reduced to Rs.121.03 at R.E. stage, and ultimately the Department of Shipping has spent
 only Rs.80.00 crore during 2004-05.  The Committee observes that actual expenditure incurred has always been low compared to the budget estimates for Inland Water Transport sector
 including North-East Pool of fund.  The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to intensify its monitoring mechanism to ensure that the budgeted amounts
 earmarked at the B.E. stage are fully utilized during 2005-06.  At the same time the Committee desires that the Department of Shipping should review all the on-going schemes and if
 required, re-allocate the funds budgeted during the financial year.
 
            The Committee notes that a comprehensive Inland Water Transport policy has been announced by the Government to encourage investment from the Private-Public participation
 for accelerated development of Inland Water Transport sector.  The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Department of Shipping for creating transparent, hospitable and conducive
 environment for ensuring both the Private and Public sector participation in the development of Inland Water Transport sector.  The Committee expects that primarily public investment in
 Inland Water Transport sector will definitely help to create infrastructure facilities and augment Inland Water Transport fleet.  The Committee recommends that all pending Inland Water
 Transport specific projects should be cleared expeditiously.

 viable routes for development of Inland Water Transport sector has not been given due consideration.  The Committee is of the view that Research & Development activities is the

 the country.
